A multi-user workflow engine in which every brick is an ephemeral OCI container and every workflow is a YAML file, versioned alongside the code it serves.

§

Get started

A workflow runs on your machine with agk run --local, and on a server with agk push and agk run --namespace. This chapter does both: a first workflow on your machine, then the same workflow on a server started with Docker Compose. Every output below is what a terminal answered at v0.2.5, not what the rest of this documentation promises.

What you need

ToolWhy
Docker daemonRuns the bricks, which are containers. Docker Desktop on macOS or Windows, Docker on Linux.
Homebrew, or Go 1.27Homebrew builds agk from the tagged source; go install does the same without it.
gitA workflow is a git repository. A local one, with no remote, is enough.
For the server part, a Linux machine with Docker Engine 28 and Compose 2.24A server runs its steps on a runner, and a runner is a Linux host (Install a server).

Install the command line

install
$ brew trust agentiik/tap
$ brew install agentiik/tap/agk
$ agk --version
agk v0.2.5, d2f1e8ba6a0dceec92962ae00de1f0d1c15e5bf4, go1.27.1

Homebrew loads the formulae of a third-party tap only once that tap is trusted, hence brew trust first. Without Homebrew: go install github.com/agentiik/agentiik/cmd/agk@v0.2.5. The formula also embeds the static helper a script step mounts at /agk/bin/agk, which a plain go install leaves out (Running a script instead of a brick).

agk alone prints its verbs, the table in Command line.

Start a workflow repository

agentiik.yaml at the root is the entry point. The rest of the repository is yours, and every step of every run sees it, mounted read-only at /agk/repo.

a directory and a file
$ mkdir first-run && cd first-run && git init
$ cat > agentiik.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: agentiik.dev/v1
kind: Workflow

metadata:
  name: first-run
  namespace: demo

outputs:
  greeting:
    from: { step: greet, port: out }

steps:
  greet:
    image: alpine:3.21
    script:
      - echo "hello from ${AGK_STEP}"
    outputs: [out]
EOF
KeyWhat it does
metadataThe workflow's namespace and name, demo/first-run in the output. On a server they say where it lives and who may see it.
steps.greet.imageAny image. A brick is an image with a manifest at /agk/brick.yaml; a script step needs none.
steps.greet.scriptOne command per entry. AGK_STEP is one of the variables every container is given.
steps.greet.outputsIts ports. A script that writes nothing under /agk/out/ports/ and exits 0 publishes one item on out, its standard output under data.stdout.
outputs.greetingWhat the run hands back: one port of one step.

Validate it

agk validate
$ agk validate
demo/first-run is valid: 1 step, 0 edges, 0 declared inputs, 1 declared output
1 step held to the manifests of 0 referenced images

No daemon was needed: this workflow names no brick, so there is no manifest to read. A workflow that names a brick reads its manifest off the image, through a daemon.

Run it

agk run --local
$ agk run --local
the daemon at /Users/you/.docker/run/docker.sock speaks API 1.56 and runs linux/aarch64
user namespace remapping is off on this daemon and this runner does not require it, so the floor is lifted: a task's files are owned by a real uid on the host, root inside a container is the host's own root, and a process that escapes a container is that account rather than an unprivileged high-numbered one that maps to no real user.
this daemon applies neither an AppArmor profile nor an SELinux label to a container, which is the host's to offer, so a container is held by its namespaces, its dropped capabilities and its seccomp profile with no mandatory access control behind them.
    0.0s  greet  running
    0.4s  greet  succeeded, out 1
demo/first-run succeeded in 0.4s: 1 step, 1 container
greeting: 1 item in .agk/runs/01M3EPQAM9D02NX7A8820CA903/outputs/greeting.json
run 01M3EPQAM9D02NX7A8820CA903: .agk/runs/01M3EPQAM9D02NX7A8820CA903

The second and third lines are what your machine gives up: Docker Desktop does not remap user namespaces (Three tiers of containment), and it applies neither AppArmor nor SELinux (Settings applied to every container). --require-userns-remap holds the first floor instead, and a run on a laptop then refuses to start.

Read what came out

Everything the run produced is under .agk, beside the entry point, when it ends. The declared output is an envelope, the one shape that travels between steps:

.agk/runs/<run>/outputs/greeting.json
{
  "meta": {
    "run_id": "01M3EPQAM9D02NX7A8820CA903",
    "step": "greet",
    "port": "out",
    "attempt": 1,
    "count": 1,
    "produced_at": "2026-09-26T11:13:36.213224Z"
  },
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "01M3EPQAYNRA50Q69J7YT73CB5",
      "data": { "stdout": "hello from greet\n" },
      "files": []
    }
  ]
}

The runner minted this id because the script gave none. A brick that cares about replay derives it from the payload, so that two runs over the same input are comparable.

Add a second step

needs names the step and port to read; as names the input port it arrives on.

agentiik.yaml, with a second step
$ cat > agentiik.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: agentiik.dev/v1
kind: Workflow

metadata:
  name: first-run
  namespace: demo

outputs:
  counted:
    from: { step: count, port: out }

steps:
  greet:
    image: alpine:3.21
    script:
      - echo "hello from ${AGK_STEP}"
    outputs: [out]

  count:
    image: alpine:3.21
    needs:
      - { step: greet, port: out, as: in }
    script:
      - echo "greet published $(/agk/bin/agk items | wc -l | tr -d ' ') item"
    outputs: [out]
EOF
agk run --local, again
$ agk run --local
# the three lines about the daemon, as above
    0.0s  greet  running
    0.3s  greet  succeeded, out 1
    0.3s  count  running
    0.7s  count  succeeded, out 1
demo/first-run succeeded in 0.7s: 2 steps, 2 containers
counted: 1 item in .agk/runs/01M3EPQGDQPEZDJJA4M5ENA77V/outputs/counted.json
run 01M3EPQGDQPEZDJJA4M5ENA77V: .agk/runs/01M3EPQGDQPEZDJJA4M5ENA77V

/agk/bin/agk (agk items, agk emit, agk attach) is an optional helper, bound read-only for a script step. jq on /agk/in/<port>/envelope.json and a redirect do the same job (script steps).

agk graph, for review inside a merge request
$ agk graph --format mermaid
flowchart LR
	step_count["count<br/>script on alpine:3.21"]
	step_greet["greet<br/>script on alpine:3.21"]

	step_greet -->|"out to in"| step_count

	output_counted(["counted"])
	step_count -. "out" .-> output_counted

Run it on a server

A server is one Compose file, compose.yaml, on a Linux machine with Docker Engine 28 and Compose 2.24 or later. On that machine, in a directory of its own:

start a server
$ mkdir -p ~/agentiik && cd ~/agentiik
$ curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentiik/deploy/v0.2.5/single-host/compose.yaml
$ echo "AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 32)" > .env
$ export AGENTIIK_TOKEN="$(sed -n 's/^AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN=//p' .env)"
$ docker compose up -d --wait

--wait returns once every service is up and healthy, and fails naming the one that is not. .env holds the operator token, which agk reads as AGENTIIK_TOKEN and without which compose.yaml refuses to start. The state is kept in data/ beside compose.yaml.

Run the workflow there

On the same machine, with agk installed as above, trust the certificate the server made and name its address:

point agk at the server, in the directory of compose.yaml
$ mkdir -p trust
$ docker compose cp api:/agentiik/trust/agentiik.pem trust/
$ export SSL_CERT_DIR="$PWD/trust"
$ export AGENTIIK_SERVER=https://localhost:8443

Then, in the chapter's first-run directory, copied to this machine: a server runs a commit, so commit the workflow, push it, and run it.

push and run
$ git add agentiik.yaml && git commit -qm "A first workflow"
$ agk push --namespace demo
$ agk run --namespace demo

agk push registers the commit in the namespace demo, which the server created, and agk run --namespace demo runs it there and follows it to its end, as --local did. Install a server has the rest: another machine, a reverse proxy, the settings, upgrades, backups and more runners.

What does not work yet

WhatTodayWhy
agk login
agk whoami
agk share
agk grants		Refused by v0.2, naming what is missing.Principals arrive in v0.3.0, which serves all four.
agk brick initRefused, naming what is missing.Brick templates come from agentiik/bricks. The roadmap says which release brings them.
network: egressRefused, not opened. network: none and network: internal run.The proxy enforcing egress.allow is v0.9.0 work, once it is designed, and an open network called filtered is worse than a refusal.

What a server does not do yet, users and the console among them, is in Install a server.

§

Install a server

A server keeps workflows and runs them: it is what agk push and agk run --namespace talk to. Two ways to install one at v0.2.5:

Linux, Docker ComposeMac, Homebrew
RunsPostgreSQL, the bus, the API, the controller and a runner, each a containerThe bus, the API and the controller as one Homebrew service; PostgreSQL from Homebrew
Runs workflowsYesNo: agk push works, and a run waits for a runner, which is a Linux host
Reached fromAny machine, on port 8443This Mac alone, at https://localhost:8443
Choose itTo run workflows, for yourself or a small teamTo try the API and agk push on a Mac
Source, and its CIagentiik/deploy, single-host/agentiik/homebrew-tap

Both keep one operator token that may do everything, since v0.2 has no users (What v0.2 does not do yet).

On a Linux machine, with Docker Compose

One file, compose.yaml, is the installation: PostgreSQL, the bus, the API, the controller, a runner, and init, which prepares the rest at every start. Every command here is run, exactly as written, on a fresh Ubuntu machine by the CI of agentiik/deploy: as in Start, on a server, and behind Caddy.

What you need

WhatWhy
A Linux host, x86-64 or arm64The runner hands the Docker daemon paths on the host to bind, which the virtual machine of Docker Desktop on macOS or Windows cannot see. agk runs anywhere.
Docker Engine 28 or later, with Compose 2.24 or laterEvery component is a container, and so is every step of every workflow. Compose 2.24 reads the inline configs and the depends_on restart the file uses.
curl, openssl, git, sudoTo download the file, make a token and commit a workflow; sudo only to back up and remove what the containers wrote as root.
Ports 8443 and 4222 openThe API serves HTTPS on 8443 (AGENTIIK_PORT) and the bus listens on 4222 (AGENTIIK_BUS_PORT), both on every interface: open them to the machines that reach the installation, and nothing else. Behind a proxy, its 443 takes the place of 8443, which then listens on the loopback alone. Where 4222 is taken, AGENTIIK_BUS_PORT in .env moves the bus.
Go 1.27, or Homebrew, where you run agkTo install the command line. agk push also needs a Docker daemon, to resolve image tags to digests.
Free space beside data/postgres for a second copy of the database, when upgrading to a release that moves PostgreSQL to a new major versionpostgres-upgrade copies the cluster rather than rewriting it, so that the old one stays whole as the way back (Upgrade). It asks for the cluster's size and 128 MiB more, and refuses with less, changing nothing, since a disk filled halfway through an upgrade is full for every other service on the host too.

Start

In a directory of its own:

start
$ mkdir -p ~/agentiik && cd ~/agentiik
$ curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentiik/deploy/v0.2.5/single-host/compose.yaml
$ echo "AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 32)" > .env
$ export AGENTIIK_TOKEN="$(sed -n 's/^AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN=//p' .env)"
$ docker compose up -d --wait

--wait returns once every service is up and healthy, and fails naming the one that is not. .env holds the operator token, the one credential of a v0.2 installation, which may do everything and which agk reads as AGENTIIK_TOKEN: compose.yaml refuses to start without it. Every other setting has its default in compose.yaml, and .env.example lists them all. The state is kept in data/ beside compose.yaml, or where AGENTIIK_DATA in .env says.

On a server

Where agk or a runner on another machine reaches the installation, AGENTIIK_HOST is the name or the address it reaches it at, which the certificate is issued to:

start, reached as agentiik.example.com
$ mkdir -p ~/agentiik && cd ~/agentiik
$ curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentiik/deploy/v0.2.5/single-host/compose.yaml
$ echo "AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 32)" > .env
$ echo 'AGENTIIK_HOST=agentiik.example.com' >> .env
$ export AGENTIIK_TOKEN="$(sed -n 's/^AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN=//p' .env)"
$ docker compose up -d --wait

Where a reverse proxy terminates TLS in front of the API, Behind a reverse proxy starts it instead.

What runs

The file in full, as it is downloaded above:

compose.yaml, from agentiik/deploy
# Agentiik on one Linux host: docker compose up -d, with a .env beside this file that sets
# AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN. Every other setting is a ${AGENTIIK_...:-default} below, and .env.example
# says what each one is for. Change one in .env and run docker compose up -d again: every service
# that reads it is recreated. The state is kept in AGENTIIK_DATA, ./data beside this file by default.
# https://github.com/agentiik/deploy/tree/main/single-host is the guide.
name: agentiik

x-agentiik: &agentiik
  network_mode: host # the API, the controller and the runner reach the bus at AGENTIIK_HOST, as a runner elsewhere does
  userns_mode: host # init writes files for uid 65532, which a daemon that remaps user namespaces would map elsewhere
  restart: unless-stopped

# Each service that reads what init writes waits for it, and is restarted when a changed setting
# recreates init: the new certificate, the new operator token's hash, a fresh join token.
x-after-init: &after-init
  init: { condition: service_completed_successfully, restart: true }

services:
  # Runs at every docker compose up, before PostgreSQL: where data/postgres was written by an older
  # major version than the one below, it upgrades it with pg_upgrade and keeps the old cluster beside
  # it, as postgres-17 from 17, the way back; anything else it leaves as it is. Its log says what it did.
  postgres-upgrade:
    image: ghcr.io/agentiik/postgres-upgrade:${AGENTIIK_VERSION:-v0.3.0}
    command: [/data/postgres, "18"] # the cluster, and the major version of the postgres image below, which it upgrades it to
    network_mode: none
    userns_mode: host # the cluster belongs to uid 70, PostgreSQL's account, which a daemon that remaps user namespaces would map elsewhere
    restart: "no"
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    cap_add: [CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, SETUID, SETGID] # to rename beside the cluster as root, and run PostgreSQL as 70
    volumes:
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}:/data" # the directory holding the cluster, since the old one is kept beside it
      - "socket:/var/run/postgresql" # where a PostgreSQL killed at its stop left its socket, which tells it is not running

  postgres:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    network_mode: none # reached through its socket alone, which only init, the API, the controller and postgres-upgrade mount, so it asks no password
    userns_mode: host
    # From 18 the image keeps its cluster in 18/docker below a volume at /var/lib/postgresql. PGDATA
    # set to that volume keeps the cluster directly in data/postgres, where v0.2.5 left it and where
    # every later major version finds it, and the mount covering the volume leaves Docker none to make.
    environment: { POSTGRES_DB: agentiik, POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD: trust, PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql }
    volumes:
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/postgres:/var/lib/postgresql"
      - "socket:/var/run/postgresql"
    healthcheck: { test: pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres, interval: 2s }
    depends_on: { postgres-upgrade: { condition: service_completed_successfully } }
    stop_grace_period: 1m # time to shut down cleanly: one cut short is a crash, which the next start, or the next upgrade, has to recover from
    restart: unless-stopped

  # Runs at every docker compose up, and brings the installation in line with the settings: the
  # certificate for AGENTIIK_HOST, the keys, the bus identity, the migration, the namespace, the
  # operator token's hash and a join token for the runner. Its log says what it did.
  init:
    image: ghcr.io/agentiik/api:${AGENTIIK_VERSION:-v0.2.5}
    command: [init]
    user: "0:0" # to give each service's directory to the account that service runs as
    network_mode: none
    userns_mode: host
    restart: "no"
    depends_on: { postgres: { condition: service_healthy } }
    environment:
      AGK_INIT_DIR: /init
      AGK_INIT_HOST: ${AGENTIIK_HOST:-localhost}
      AGK_INIT_NAMESPACE: ${AGENTIIK_NAMESPACE:-demo}
      AGK_OPERATOR_TOKEN: ${AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN:?set AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN in .env to 32 characters or more, such as openssl rand -hex 32 writes}
      AGK_MIGRATE_DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres@/agentiik?host=/run/postgresql
      AGK_DATABASE_URL: postgres://agentiik@/agentiik?host=/run/postgresql
    volumes:
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/api:/init/api"
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/controller:/init/controller"
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/bus:/init/bus"
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/nats:/init/nats"
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/runner:/init/runner"
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/objects:/init/objects"
      - "socket:/run/postgresql"

  nats:
    image: nats:2-alpine
    # Not on the host's network, so that nothing it listens on inside, such as its monitoring port,
    # can collide with a program of the host: only the bus port is published, where every runner
    # reaches it.
    ports: ["${AGENTIIK_BUS_PORT:-4222}:4222"]
    userns_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["-c", "/nats/nats.conf"] # written by init: 4222 on every interface, over TLS alone
    depends_on: *after-init
    volumes:
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/nats:/nats"
    healthcheck: { test: wget -qO /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8222/healthz, interval: 2s }

  api:
    <<: *agentiik
    image: ghcr.io/agentiik/api:${AGENTIIK_VERSION:-v0.2.5}
    depends_on: { <<: *after-init, nats: { condition: service_healthy } }
    environment:
      AGK_DATABASE_URL: postgres://agentiik@/agentiik?host=/run/postgresql
      AGK_DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE: /agentiik/database-password
      AGK_BUS_URL: tls://${AGENTIIK_HOST:-localhost}:${AGENTIIK_BUS_PORT:-4222} # the address every runner is handed too, on the certificate
      AGK_BUS_CREDENTIALS_FILE: /bus/control-plane.creds # the API renews it here, 14 days before its end; the controller reads it
      AGK_BUS_ACCOUNT_SEED_FILE: /agentiik/bus/account.seed
      AGK_OBJECTS_DIR: /objects
      AGK_PRESIGN_KEY_FILE: /agentiik/presign-key
      AGK_MASTER_KEY_FILE: /agentiik/master-key # the API's alone: the controller refuses to start with it
      AGK_OPERATOR_TOKEN_FILE: /agentiik/operator-token.sha256
      AGK_LISTEN: :${AGENTIIK_PORT:-8443}
      AGK_PUBLIC_URL: https://${AGENTIIK_HOST:-localhost}:${AGENTIIK_PORT:-8443}
      AGK_TLS_CERT_FILE: /agentiik/tls/server.pem
      AGK_TLS_KEY_FILE: /agentiik/tls/server.key
      # Set, the API is reached at the proxy's URL and serves plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 alone, leaving
      # the two lines above and the certificate unread.
      AGK_PROXY_URL: ${AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL:-}
      SSL_CERT_DIR: /agentiik/trust # the certificate init made, beside the system's authorities
    volumes:
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/api:/agentiik"
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/bus:/bus"
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/objects:/objects"
      - "socket:/run/postgresql"
    healthcheck: { test: [CMD, /agentiik-api, health], interval: 2s } # the image has no shell, hence the exec form

  controller:
    <<: *agentiik
    image: ghcr.io/agentiik/controller:${AGENTIIK_VERSION:-v0.2.5}
    depends_on: { <<: *after-init, nats: { condition: service_healthy } }
    environment:
      AGK_DATABASE_URL: postgres://agentiik@/agentiik?host=/run/postgresql
      AGK_DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE: /agentiik/database-password
      AGK_BUS_URL: tls://${AGENTIIK_HOST:-localhost}:${AGENTIIK_BUS_PORT:-4222}
      AGK_BUS_CREDENTIALS_FILE: /bus/control-plane.creds
      AGK_OBJECTS_DIR: /objects
      SSL_CERT_DIR: /agentiik/trust
    volumes:
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/controller:/agentiik"
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/bus:/bus:ro"
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/objects:/objects"
      - "socket:/run/postgresql"

  # Started as root, it takes the group of the Docker socket, drops to uid 65532 and serves, joining
  # the pool default with the token init wrote where it has no identity yet, or where AGK_API changed.
  runner:
    <<: *agentiik
    image: ghcr.io/agentiik/runner:${AGENTIIK_VERSION:-v0.2.5}
    depends_on: { <<: *after-init, api: { condition: service_healthy } }
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    cap_add: [CHOWN, FOWNER, DAC_OVERRIDE, SETUID, SETGID]
    environment:
      AGK_API: ${AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL:-https://${AGENTIIK_HOST:-localhost}:${AGENTIIK_PORT:-8443}}
      AGK_RUNNER_CONCURRENCY: ${AGENTIIK_RUNNER_CONCURRENCY:-2}
      AGK_RUNNER_JOIN_TOKEN_FILE: /etc/agentiik/join-token
      SSL_CERT_DIR: /etc/agentiik/trust:/etc/ssl/agentiik # init's certificate, and AGENTIIK_CA
    labels:
      # What the runner reads from the files below, here too so that a change to either recreates it.
      dev.agentiik.require-userns-remap: ${AGENTIIK_REQUIRE_USERNS_REMAP:-false}
      dev.agentiik.ca: ${AGENTIIK_CA:-}
    configs:
      - { source: runner-toml, target: /etc/agentiik/runner.toml }
      - { source: ca, target: /etc/ssl/agentiik/ca.pem }
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/runner:/etc/agentiik" # init's certificate and join token, and the identity join writes
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/runner-state:/var/lib/agentiik" # the runner's key and credential
      # The work root, at the same path on both sides, since the daemon resolves the bind sources
      # of every step's container on this host. The one path outside AGENTIIK_DATA this file names.
      - /var/lib/agentiik/work:/var/lib/agentiik/work

configs:
  runner-toml:
    content: |
      # false gives up the floor on a daemon that does not remap user namespaces: root in a step's
      # container is then root on this host. Remap the daemon and set AGENTIIK_REQUIRE_USERNS_REMAP=true.
      require_userns_remap = ${AGENTIIK_REQUIRE_USERNS_REMAP:-false}
  ca:
    # Never empty, since Compose takes a config with no content for a file to bind.
    content: |
      # AGENTIIK_CA: authorities the runner trusts beside the system's, such as a proxy's own.
      ${AGENTIIK_CA:-}

# PostgreSQL's socket, which is no data to keep: a Docker volume rather than a directory of
# AGENTIIK_DATA, since some file systems a host shares with Docker cannot hold a socket.
volumes:
  socket:

postgres-upgrade and init run first at every docker compose up, and the other services wait for them. postgres-upgrade upgrades PostgreSQL's data where a release moves it to a new major version, and leaves it as it is otherwise (Upgrade). init brings the installation in line with .env, so a setting changed is applied at the next start and none is read at the first start alone:

WhatThe first timeAt every later start
The certificateMade for AGENTIIK_HOST, localhost and 127.0.0.1, ECDSA P-256, valid 825 days.Kept while it names the host, has not expired and is its key's; made again where AGENTIIK_HOST changed or it expired. One a person put there is never replaced: init refuses to start instead, saying what to do.
The master key, the presign key, the database passwordMade.Kept: they are not settings, and a new one would be an installation that no longer reads what it wrote.
The bus identityMade, as bus-init makes it.Kept. The control plane's credential, valid 90 days, is in data/bus, and is renewed from 14 days before its end, by the API and by init.
The databaseMigrated.Migrated: what a new version adds.
AGENTIIK_NAMESPACECreated.Created where it is new; a previous one stays.
A join token for the runnerIssued for the pool default, valid an hour.Issued again, since the runner may have to join again after a setting changed; it uses one only where it has to.
The operator tokenThe hash of AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN.The hash of AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN, written where it differs.
docker compose ps --all
$ docker compose ps --all
NAME                          IMAGE                                      COMMAND                  SERVICE            STATUS
agentiik-api-1                ghcr.io/agentiik/api:v0.2.5                "/agentiik-api serve"    api                Up (healthy)
agentiik-controller-1         ghcr.io/agentiik/controller:v0.2.5         "/agentiik-controller"   controller         Up
agentiik-init-1               ghcr.io/agentiik/api:v0.2.5                "/agentiik-api init"     init               Exited (0)
agentiik-nats-1               nats:2-alpine                              "docker-entrypoint.s…"   nats               Up (healthy)
agentiik-postgres-1           postgres:18-alpine                         "docker-entrypoint.s…"   postgres           Up (healthy)
agentiik-postgres-upgrade-1   ghcr.io/agentiik/postgres-upgrade:v0.3.0   "/usr/local/bin/post…"   postgres-upgrade   Exited (0)
agentiik-runner-1             ghcr.io/agentiik/runner:v0.2.5             "/usr/local/bin/agk-…"   runner             Up

postgres-upgrade and init have done their work when they have Exited (0); docker compose logs and a service's name say what it did, or why a service is not up. Everything the installation keeps is in data/, one directory per service, and the one other path it uses on the host is /var/lib/agentiik/work, where the runner lays out each step's files for the daemon to bind. PostgreSQL's socket is the one Docker volume, since it is no data to keep and some file systems cannot hold a socket.

Point agk at it

install agk, and trust the certificate init made
$ go install github.com/agentiik/agentiik/cmd/agk@v0.2.5
$ export PATH="$PATH:$(go env GOPATH)/bin"
$ mkdir -p trust
$ docker compose cp api:/agentiik/trust/agentiik.pem trust/
$ export SSL_CERT_DIR="$PWD/trust"

brew install agentiik/tap/agk installs the same command line. SSL_CERT_DIR adds the certificate init made to the authorities agk trusts on Linux. AGENTIIK_SERVER is the address, and CURL_CA_BUNDLE what curl trusts there:

started as in Start
$ export AGENTIIK_SERVER=https://localhost:8443
$ export CURL_CA_BUNDLE="$PWD/trust/agentiik.pem"
with AGENTIIK_HOST set
$ export AGENTIIK_SERVER=https://agentiik.example.com:8443
$ export CURL_CA_BUNDLE="$PWD/trust/agentiik.pem"

From another machine

AGENTIIK_HOST in .env is the name the other machine reaches this one at. AGENTIIK_SERVER is then https:// that name :8443, or AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL behind a reverse proxy, and AGENTIIK_TOKEN the operator token in .env. The certificate is trust/agentiik.pem, which docker compose cp copied out above. Copy it to that machine and trust it: SSL_CERT_DIR naming its directory on Linux, and on macOS:

macOS: agk trusts what the keychain trusts
$ sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain agentiik.pem

From v0.3.0, a browser signing in with a passkey has to trust the certificate the same way, since it runs no passkey ceremony on a page clicked past a warning (The sign-in page); a reverse proxy with a certificate from a public authority spares the step.

Run a first workflow

A workflow is a git repository with an agentiik.yaml at its root, with one line on standard error for agk logs to show and one file for curl to fetch:

push, run, read
$ mkdir -p ~/first-run && cd ~/first-run && git init -q
$ cat > agentiik.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: agentiik.dev/v1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: first-run
  namespace: demo
outputs:
  greeting:
    from: { step: greet, port: out }
    retain: 7d
steps:
  greet:
    image: alpine:3.21
    script:
      - echo "greet runs on $(uname -m)" >&2
      - echo "hello from ${AGK_STEP}"
      - echo "a file from ${AGK_STEP}" > /agk/out/files/greeting.txt
    outputs: [out]
EOF
$ git add agentiik.yaml && git commit -qm "A first workflow"
$ agk push --namespace demo
$ agk run --namespace demo 2>&1 | tee ~/first-run.log
$ run=$(awk '/ started at / { print $2; exit }' ~/first-run.log)
$ agk status "$run"
$ agk logs "$run"
$ curl -fsSL -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTIIK_TOKEN" "$AGENTIIK_SERVER/api/v1/artifacts/agk%3A%2F%2Frun%2F$run%2Fgreet%2Fout%2Fgreeting.txt"
$ cd ~/agentiik
what agk push, run, status and logs print, then curl
user namespace remapping is off on this daemon and this runner does not require it, so the floor is lifted: ...
alpine:3.21 resolved to alpine@sha256:ce64758a109eb420d874a118f87920e625e12d3634e03b4a5573fd9f6e5d3507
demo/first-run@9d4e925 pushed to https://localhost:8443
1 step, 1 file, 0 included files, 0 manifests, 1 tag resolved to its digest
run 01M3EF42G80SR9XW17YWGEYTTT of demo/first-run@9d4e925 started at https://localhost:8443
    0.6s  greet  succeeded, out 1
first-run succeeded in 0.6s: 1 step, 1 container
greeting: 1 item
run 01M3EF42G80SR9XW17YWGEYTTT: https://localhost:8443/api/v1/demo/runs/01M3EF42G80SR9XW17YWGEYTTT
run 01M3EF42G80SR9XW17YWGEYTTT: demo/first-run@9d4e925, succeeded after 0.6s
manual by operator at 2026-09-26T09:00:44Z
greet  succeeded, out 1 sha256:2ec2167f189f
output greeting: 1 item
greet | greet runs on x86_64
greet | driver: the container exited 0: the output envelopes are published
a file from greet
CommandDoes
agk push --namespace demoRegisters the committed workflow in the namespace demo, which init created, each image tag resolved to its digest on your own Docker daemon: hence the first line.
agk run --namespace demoStarts a run of HEAD on the server and follows it to its end. An interrupt stops the following, not the run.
agk status <run>How the run and each step stand, and the digest of each output.
agk logs <run>What each step wrote on standard error. What it wrote on standard output became its output.
curlFetches the file the step left in /agk/out/files/, an artifact of its output kept for the seven days retain says, by its URI agk://run/<run>/greet/out/greeting.txt, percent-encoded as one segment of the path.

Change a setting

Every setting but the operator token has its default in compose.yaml. This file says what each one is for; uncomment a line in .env, then run docker compose up -d again:

.env.example, from agentiik/deploy
# Save as .env beside compose.yaml and fill AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN, the one required line. Every
# other setting has its default in compose.yaml: uncomment what you change, then docker compose up -d,
# and every service that reads a changed setting is recreated, and init brings the installation in line.

# The operator token, which may do everything: 32 characters or more, such as openssl rand -hex 32
# writes. Only its hash is written anywhere else. Changed, the previous one stops working.
AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN=

# Where the installation keeps its state, one directory per service: ./data beside compose.yaml,
# or an absolute path such as /srv/agentiik on a server. Back it up; it holds the master key.
#AGENTIIK_DATA=./data

# The version of Agentiik, one for every image; compose.yaml names its own release. To upgrade, download the new release's compose.yaml rather than changing this alone, since a release may change the services too.
#AGENTIIK_VERSION=v0.2.5

# The name agk and every runner reach the installation at: a DNS name or an IPv4 address, which the
# certificate init makes is issued to. localhost is enough on one machine; a runner on another machine
# needs a name or an address it reaches. Changed, init issues a new certificate, which clients trust.
#AGENTIIK_HOST=localhost

# The port the API serves HTTPS on, on every interface. Behind a proxy, plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 alone.
#AGENTIIK_PORT=8443

# The port the bus listens on, on every interface, which every runner reaches. Change it where 4222 is taken.
#AGENTIIK_BUS_PORT=4222

# The https URL of a reverse proxy on this host that terminates TLS in front of the API, such as
# https://agentiik.example.com. Unset, the API serves TLS itself at https://AGENTIIK_HOST:AGENTIIK_PORT.
# The bus is not proxied, and keeps its own TLS on AGENTIIK_BUS_PORT at AGENTIIK_HOST.
#AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL=

# The namespace init creates, where workflows are pushed and run. Changed, the previous one stays.
#AGENTIIK_NAMESPACE=demo

# How many tasks the runner holds at once. Kept low, since it shares this host with PostgreSQL.
#AGENTIIK_RUNNER_CONCURRENCY=2

# false lets the runner use a Docker daemon that does not remap user namespaces, where root in a
# step's container is root on this host. true keeps that floor, and needs userns-remap on the daemon.
#AGENTIIK_REQUIRE_USERNS_REMAP=false

# Certificates the runner trusts beside the system's authorities, in PEM, in double quotes over as many
# lines as it takes: the authority of the proxy in front, where the system does not trust it.
#AGENTIIK_CA="-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
#...
#-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
Changed in .envAt the next docker compose up -d
AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKENRequired. The new token works and the previous one stops working.
AGENTIIK_DATAThe state is read and written there: a new, empty directory is a new installation. Move data/ there first, with the installation stopped, to keep it.
AGENTIIK_VERSIONEvery image is that version's, and init migrates the database before the API and the controller start on them.
AGENTIIK_HOSTA new certificate, which clients trust in place of the previous one. The runner, handed a new address, joins again as a new runner.
AGENTIIK_PORTThe API listens there, and the runner joins again at the new address.
AGENTIIK_BUS_PORTThe bus is published there, and every runner is handed the new address.
AGENTIIK_PROXY_URLThe API is reached at the proxy's URL and serves plain HTTP on the loopback (Behind a reverse proxy); the runner joins again at that URL.
AGENTIIK_NAMESPACECreated beside the previous one, which stays.
AGENTIIK_RUNNER_CONCURRENCY, AGENTIIK_REQUIRE_USERNS_REMAP, AGENTIIK_CAThe runner starts again with them.

A second namespace, and a new operator token, which stops the previous one working:

change two settings
$ echo 'AGENTIIK_NAMESPACE=team' >> .env
$ sed -i '/^AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN=/d' .env
$ echo "AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 32)" >> .env
$ docker compose up -d --wait
$ export AGENTIIK_TOKEN="$(sed -n 's/^AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN=//p' .env)"

A runner that joins again is a new runner, and the one it was stays registered until an administrator revokes it: the API checked the address and the labels against the token when they were claimed, so an identity cannot follow a change to either. docker compose restart does not read .env again, so it applies nothing. The token is AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN rather than AGENTIIK_TOKEN, which agk reads, because Compose prefers a variable of the shell to the same one in .env: exported for agk, it would hide every change made in .env. Another namespace is also docker compose run --rm --no-deps api namespace create NAME, which leaves .env as it is.

Upgrade

Download the new release's compose.yaml in place of the old one, since a release may change the services as well as their version, and keep .env; remove AGENTIIK_VERSION from .env if it pins the old one. Then:

upgrade
$ docker compose up -d --wait
  • init migrates the database before the API and the controller start again on the new images. agk is upgraded the way it was installed.
  • Where a release moves PostgreSQL to a new major version, as v0.3.0 moves it from 17 to 18, postgres-upgrade upgrades data/postgres with pg_upgrade in copy mode before PostgreSQL starts, and keeps the previous cluster beside it as data/postgres-17, as the previous release left it: the way back, for you to remove once you no longer need it. A PostgreSQL the previous release left without shutting down, killed at the end of its grace, is recovered first. A failure at any step leaves data/postgres as it was, removes what was built beside it, and says why in docker compose logs postgres-upgrade; PostgreSQL then does not start, and the next docker compose up takes the upgrade up again. The same service carries every later major version.
  • Upgrading to v0.3.0 also settles what v0.2 left on the disk, with nothing to do by hand. A run v0.2 finished carries no expiry: migration 0038 gives its envelopes and logs its namespace's max_retention_days from its end. The artifact files v0.2 recorded nothing for, those of every output given no retain, are recorded by init from the envelopes of those runs, each expiring its namespace's max_retention_days after its run finished, and what init leaves the controller records. The purges then retire them and the collection deletes them, so an upgraded installation's store shrinks on its own.
  • From v0.2.5, a release starts on the state the one before it left, with compose.yaml and .env changed and nothing else: init applies every change at docker compose up (migrations, file layout, credentials), and a setting keeps its name or is still read under its old one. A check on every change of agentiik/deploy installs the latest release, runs a workflow, upgrades, and finds the old run and token still working and a new run succeeding; the same from latest to dev.
  • Upgrading to v0.3.0 from v0.2.5's compose.yaml, which requires the token, keeps AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN working, as the bootstrap token, until the first administrator can sign in to a full session, with a passkey or a password (First run). It then stops, the line stays in .env and init says at every run that it is ignored, and a script moves to a service account's token. A run it started that has not been let in by then ends cancelled, naming the end; one already running goes on.
  • An installation of v0.2.4 kept its state in Docker volumes rather than data/, and one made with setup, up to v0.2.3, in /srv/agentiik: neither is upgraded in place. Remove it as its own guide said, then start anew.
  • The bus credential of the API and the controller lasts 90 days. The API renews it itself from 14 days before its end, in data/bus, which it shares with the controller, and both take the new one with no restart; it warns daily only where it cannot. init renews it too at any docker compose up in that time.

Back up

The database and data/, taken together, since a run restored without its objects points at artifacts that no longer exist. The database is dumped rather than copied, since its files copied while it runs may not restore. Where .env sets AGENTIIK_DATA, that directory takes the place of data here and below:

back up
$ docker compose exec -T postgres pg_dump -U postgres -Fc agentiik > agentiik.dump
$ sudo tar -czf agentiik-data.tar.gz --exclude='data/postgres*' data

The archive leaves out data/postgres, which the dump holds in a form that restores, and a cluster an upgrade kept beside it, data/postgres-17. It holds the master key, which opens every secret in the dump: keep the two apart, or encrypt them.

Remove

Every container, image and key, and the state, which the containers wrote as root:

remove
$ docker compose down --rmi all --volumes
$ sudo rm -rf data /var/lib/agentiik/work

Behind Caddy, docker rm --force caddy && docker volume rm caddy-data too.

Behind a reverse proxy

The proxy holds the TLS certificate and serves the API on 443; the API serves plain HTTP on the loopback, for the proxy alone; the bus keeps its own TLS on 4222 and is not proxied, since it speaks NATS rather than HTTP.

Without a proxyBehind a proxy
The APIHTTPS on :8443, every interface, with the certificate init makesPlain HTTP on 127.0.0.1:8443 (AGENTIIK_PORT), for the proxy to forward to
The proxyNoneHTTPS on :443, with a certificate of its own: Let's Encrypt, or its own authority
The busNATS over TLS on :4222 (AGENTIIK_BUS_PORT), with the certificate init makesThe same
agk and runners reach the API athttps://AGENTIIK_HOST:8443AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL, which every presigned URL is minted on too
They trust, for the APItrust/agentiik.pemThe system's own authorities, or trust/proxy.pem where the proxy's authority is not one of them, which AGENTIIK_CA hands the runner
Runners trust, for the busagentiik.pemagentiik.pem
Open to other machines8443 and 4222443 and 4222; 8443 listens on the loopback alone

AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL in .env chooses it, and the API then leaves its certificate unread, so the same compose.yaml serves both ways. AGENTIIK_HOST stays the name runners reach the bus at, usually the same one. With Caddy, in a container on this host:

Caddy in front
$ mkdir -p ~/agentiik && cd ~/agentiik
$ curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentiik/deploy/v0.2.5/single-host/compose.yaml
$ curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentiik/deploy/v0.2.5/single-host/proxy/Caddyfile
$ echo "AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 32)" > .env
$ echo 'AGENTIIK_HOST=agentiik.example.com' >> .env
$ echo 'AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL=https://agentiik.example.com' >> .env
$ docker run --detach --name caddy --restart unless-stopped --network host -e AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL=https://agentiik.example.com \
  -v "$PWD/Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro" -v caddy-data:/data caddy:2

Where the proxy's certificate is from an authority the system does not trust, such as Caddy's own for an IP address or a name like agentiik.internal, AGENTIIK_CA hands it to the runner, and trust/ keeps it for agk and curl. Then start:

trust the proxy's authority, and start
$ mkdir -p trust
$ docker exec caddy sh -c 'until [ -s /data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt ]; do sleep 1; done; cat /data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt' > trust/proxy.pem
$ echo "AGENTIIK_CA=\"$(cat trust/proxy.pem)\"" >> .env
$ export AGENTIIK_TOKEN="$(sed -n 's/^AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN=//p' .env)"
$ docker compose up -d --wait
point agk at the proxy
$ mkdir -p trust
$ docker compose cp api:/agentiik/trust/agentiik.pem trust/
$ export SSL_CERT_DIR="$PWD/trust"
$ export AGENTIIK_SERVER=https://agentiik.example.com
$ export CURL_CA_BUNDLE="$PWD/trust/proxy.pem"

The rest is as without a proxy, from a first workflow on, with the variables set above.

Caddy, nginx or Traefik

ProxyFiles in proxy/Where they go
CaddyCaddyfileMounted as above, with AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL in Caddy's environment. Caddy obtains and renews the certificate itself.
nginxnginx.conf/etc/nginx/conf.d/agentiik.conf, with your name and certificate in place of agentiik.example.com.
Traefiktraefik.yaml, traefik-agentiik.yaml/etc/traefik/, with your name and an address for Let's Encrypt in place of the examples.

Each sets what the API needs of a proxy, where the proxy's default does not already give it:

The API needsBecauseCaddynginxTraefik
A log stream passed on as it is writtenA step's log is server-sent eventsflush_interval -1proxy_buffering offits default
The path passed undecodedAn artifact's URI is one segment whose slashes are %2Fits defaultproxy_pass with no path after the addressallowEncodedSlash: true
No body size limitA runner uploads artifacts of up to 5 GiB, and the API bounds each route itselfits defaultclient_max_body_size 0, and proxy_request_buffering off to stream itits default
No timeout under an hourA download has an hour, and a log stream lasts as long as its stepits defaultproxy_read_timeout 1h, proxy_send_timeout 1hreadTimeout: 0, for uploads

From v0.3.0 the API reads one header the proxy writes, X-Forwarded-For, for one thing: the address a sign-in comes from, which the audit log records and the counts of failed sign-ins and of password attempts are kept by. It takes the header's last entry, the one the proxy wrote after whatever its client sent, and reads it only behind AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL, since the API then listens on the loopback and nothing but the proxy reaches it; where no entry reads as an address, the connection's, the proxy's own, is taken. Caddy and Traefik write it by default. nginx writes it only where told to, and the nginx.conf below, agentiik/deploy's as it stands, does not tell it yet: add proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr; to its location /. Without it every sign-in counts as the proxy's address, and one whose client wrote the header itself as whatever that client chose. Every address the API hands out is minted on AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL. The CI of agentiik/deploy runs the install above behind Caddy, and each of these files in front of a stand-in that checks the first three rows.

proxy/Caddyfile, from agentiik/deploy
# Caddy in front of the single-host installation. It serves the address AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL names,
# from the environment, with a certificate it obtains and renews: from Let's Encrypt for a public
# name, from its own authority for an IP address or a name such as agentiik.internal.
{$AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL} {
	# The API, in plain HTTP on the loopback: AGENTIIK_PORT in .env.
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8443 {
		# Every write passed on at once, so that a step's log stream (server-sent events) is
		# never held back. Caddy already does it for text/event-stream; this says so.
		flush_interval -1
	}
	# Nothing else to set: Caddy passes the path as sent, %2F included, sets no request body
	# limit and no response timeout, and the API reads no X-Forwarded-* header.
}
proxy/nginx.conf, from agentiik/deploy: /etc/nginx/conf.d/agentiik.conf
# nginx in front of the single-host installation: a server block for /etc/nginx/conf.d/, with the
# name AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL names and a certificate for it, from certbot for example.
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    listen [::]:443 ssl;
    server_name agentiik.example.com;
    ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/agentiik.example.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/agentiik.example.com/privkey.pem;

    # A push is up to 16 MiB and an artifact a runner uploads up to 5 GiB: no limit here, since
    # the API holds each route to its own. nginx's default is 1 MiB.
    client_max_body_size 0;

    location / {
        # No path after the address, so nginx passes the path as the client sent it: an artifact's
        # URI is one segment with its slashes as %2F, which a decoded path would split.
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8443;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;

        # A step's log stream (server-sent events) goes out as it is written. The API also says
        # so with X-Accel-Buffering: no; uploads stream to the API rather than to a temporary file.
        proxy_buffering off;
        proxy_request_buffering off;

        # An artifact has an hour to download, and a log stream lasts as long as its step, with a
        # comment every 15 seconds in between. nginx's default is 60 seconds.
        proxy_read_timeout 1h;
        proxy_send_timeout 1h;
    }
}
proxy/traefik.yaml, from agentiik/deploy: /etc/traefik/traefik.yaml
# Traefik in front of the single-host installation: its static configuration, as
# /etc/traefik/traefik.yaml, with traefik-agentiik.yaml beside it for the route.
entryPoints:
  websecure:
    address: ":443"
    transport:
      respondingTimeouts:
        # Traefik v3 stops reading a request after 60 seconds, which cuts an artifact upload of
        # up to 5 GiB short: 0 is no limit. The API bounds what it reads on each route.
        readTimeout: 0
    http:
      encodedCharacters:
        # An artifact's URI is one path segment with its slashes as %2F, which Traefik refuses
        # by default. It reaches the API undecoded.
        allowEncodedSlash: true

providers:
  file:
    filename: /etc/traefik/traefik-agentiik.yaml

certificatesResolvers:
  letsencrypt:
    acme:
      email: admin@example.com
      storage: /etc/traefik/acme.json
      tlsChallenge: {}
proxy/traefik-agentiik.yaml, from agentiik/deploy: /etc/traefik/traefik-agentiik.yaml
# Traefik's route to the single-host installation, which traefik.yaml reads with its file provider.
http:
  routers:
    agentiik:
      rule: Host(`agentiik.example.com`) # the name AGENTIIK_PROXY_URL names
      entryPoints: [websecure]
      service: agentiik
      tls:
        certResolver: letsencrypt
  services:
    agentiik:
      loadBalancer:
        servers:
          - url: http://127.0.0.1:8443 # the API, in plain HTTP on the loopback: AGENTIIK_PORT in .env
        # Nothing else to set: Traefik streams server-sent events as they come, passes the body
        # whole with no size limit, and the API reads no X-Forwarded-* header.

A runner on another machine

It joins as in Add a runner on another machine, with two differences: AGENTIIK_API in its .env is the proxy's URL, https://agentiik.example.com, and AGENTIIK_CA holds every certificate in trust/, agentiik.pem for the bus and proxy.pem where there is one for the API. It reaches 443 and 4222; nothing connects to it.

On a Mac, with Homebrew

The API, the controller and the bus on this Mac, reached at https://localhost:8443 from this Mac alone. A runner is a Linux host, so workflows are pushed here and a run waits. The install, the start, the check, agk push, the stop and the removal are run by the CI of agentiik/homebrew-tap on macOS.

What you need

WhatWhy
macOS with HomebrewThe formula builds the programs from the tagged source.
PostgreSQL 17 from HomebrewThe database. The service does not run it, so any PostgreSQL answering on /tmp will do. The programs run on 17 and 18 alike; Homebrew's server stays on 17 in v0.3.0, where the Compose installation moves to 18, since moving a server's data from one postgresql@ formula to the next is a piece of work of its own.
Your password, onceagentiik-setup adds the certificate's authority to the System keychain: the programs, agk included, trust what macOS trusts.
Ports 8443 and 4222 free on the loopbackThe API and the bus.

Install and start

install
$ brew trust agentiik/tap
$ brew install agentiik/tap/agentiik postgresql@17
$ brew services start postgresql@17
$ agentiik-setup
$ brew services start agentiik/tap/agentiik

agentiik-setup writes the secrets, the certificate, the database, a namespace named after you with agentiik-api namespace create (--namespace to choose) and the bus identity, then prints the two lines that point agk at the server, export AGENTIIK_SERVER=https://localhost:8443 and export AGENTIIK_TOKEN= the operator token, shown this once. From v0.3.0 that is the bootstrap token, which it keeps in operator-token.env, readable by you alone, as .env keeps it for Compose, and a later run prints a line reading it from there. Run again, it keeps all of that and repairs what is missing. brew services start runs the bus, the API and the controller, and again at every login; from v0.3.0 it first runs agentiik-api migrate, at every start, which applies the release's migrations and keeps the bootstrap token's hash, as init does for Compose, and, given AGK_OBJECTS_DIR from api.env, records the artifact files a v0.2 server left unrecorded, for the purges to expire and collect.

Check it is up

the API answers the operator
$ export AGENTIIK_SERVER=https://localhost:8443
$ export AGENTIIK_TOKEN=<the token agentiik-setup printed>
$ curl --cacert "$(brew --prefix)/etc/agentiik/tls/ca.pem" -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTIIK_TOKEN" "$AGENTIIK_SERVER/api/v1/runner-pools"
$ agk push --namespace <the namespace it named>
# from a workflow's repository

curl reads its own list of authorities rather than the keychain, hence --cacert. The logs are in $(brew --prefix)/var/log/agentiik, one file per program.

Stop, restart, upgrade, back up, remove

operate
# stop, and start again
$ brew services stop agentiik/tap/agentiik
$ brew services restart agentiik/tap/agentiik

# upgrade, to v0.3.0 and after: the service migrates at every start
$ brew upgrade agentiik/tap/agentiik
$ brew services restart agentiik/tap/agentiik

# back up: the database and the files, taken together
$ "$(brew --prefix postgresql@17)/bin/pg_dump" -h /tmp -Fc agentiik > agentiik.dump
$ tar -C "$(brew --prefix)" -czf agentiik-files.tar.gz etc/agentiik var/lib/agentiik

# another namespace
$ agentiik-setup --namespace team

# remove the database, the secrets and the keychain entry, then the programs
$ brew services stop agentiik/tap/agentiik
$ agentiik-setup remove --yes
$ brew uninstall agentiik/tap/agentiik
$ rm -rf "$(brew --prefix)/etc/agentiik" "$(brew --prefix)/var/log/agentiik"

The settings are files in $(brew --prefix)/etc/agentiik, api.env, controller.env, nats-server.conf and, from v0.3.0, operator-token.env, the bootstrap token as AGK_OPERATOR_TOKEN=, mode 0600, which the service hands to migrate alone since every other program refuses it. Homebrew keeps them across upgrades; Configuration says what each setting is.

A server set up by v0.2 has no operator-token.env: its token's hash is in secrets/operator-token.sha256, which api.env names in AGK_OPERATOR_TOKEN_FILE, and the first start of v0.3.0 imports it once, so the token agentiik-setup printed then works on as the bootstrap token with brew upgrade and a restart alone.

Add a runner on another machine

Any Linux machine with Docker Engine 28 and Compose 2.24 can run steps for the Compose installation, as long as it reaches AGENTIIK_HOST on 4222, and the API on 8443 or the proxy's 443; nothing connects to it. It joins a pool with a single-use token the operator issues, and takes the steps whose runs_on names its labels. It is one Compose file of its own and a .env. The CI of agentiik/deploy runs these commands, the other machine included.

on the installation's host: a pool for the new machine's label, and a join token for it, valid an hour
$ curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTIIK_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"pool":{"name":"lab","labels":["zone=lab"],"namespaces":[],"resource_ceilings":{}}}' "$AGENTIIK_SERVER/api/v1/runner-pools"
$ JOIN_TOKEN=$(curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTIIK_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"labels":["zone=lab"]}' "$AGENTIIK_SERVER/api/v1/runner-pools/lab/join-tokens" | sed -n 's/.*"token" *: *"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
$ echo "$JOIN_TOKEN"

On the other machine, in a directory of its own, the certificates in trust/ on the installation's host: agentiik.pem, which the bus serves and, with no proxy in front, the API, and proxy.pem where the proxy's authority is one the system does not trust. Then the installation's address as that machine reaches it, and the token:

on the other machine
$ AGENTIIK_SERVER=https://agentiik.example.com:8443
$ JOIN_TOKEN=agkjoin_...

Behind a proxy, AGENTIIK_SERVER is its URL, https://agentiik.example.com. The runner's own Compose file:

runner/compose.yaml, from agentiik/deploy
# An Agentiik runner on a Linux machine of its own, for an installation elsewhere: docker compose up -d,
# with a .env beside this file that names the installation, and a join token for the first start.
# .env.example says what each setting is for. Change one in .env and run docker compose up -d again.
# The state is kept in AGENTIIK_DATA, ./data beside this file by default.
# https://github.com/agentiik/deploy/tree/main/single-host#add-a-runner-on-another-machine is the guide.
name: agentiik-runner

services:
  # Started as root, it takes the group of the Docker socket, drops to uid 65532 and serves. Where
  # it has no identity yet, or where AGENTIIK_API or AGENTIIK_LABELS changed, it joins with the token.
  runner:
    image: ghcr.io/agentiik/runner:${AGENTIIK_VERSION:-v0.2.5}
    network_mode: host # the API and the bus at the addresses this machine reaches them at; the runner listens on nothing
    userns_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    cap_add: [CHOWN, FOWNER, DAC_OVERRIDE, SETUID, SETGID]
    environment:
      AGK_API: ${AGENTIIK_API:?set AGENTIIK_API in .env to the installation's address, such as https://agentiik.example.com:8443}
      AGK_RUNNER_JOIN_TOKEN: ${AGENTIIK_JOIN_TOKEN:-} # read only where the runner has to join
      AGK_RUNNER_LABELS: ${AGENTIIK_LABELS:-}
      AGK_RUNNER_CONCURRENCY: ${AGENTIIK_RUNNER_CONCURRENCY:-2}
      SSL_CERT_DIR: /etc/ssl/agentiik # AGENTIIK_CA, beside the system's authorities
    labels:
      # What the runner reads from the files below, here too so that a change to either recreates it.
      dev.agentiik.require-userns-remap: ${AGENTIIK_REQUIRE_USERNS_REMAP:-false}
      dev.agentiik.ca: ${AGENTIIK_CA:-}
    configs:
      - { source: runner-toml, target: /etc/agentiik/runner.toml }
      - { source: ca, target: /etc/ssl/agentiik/ca.pem }
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/runner:/etc/agentiik" # the identity join writes
      - "${AGENTIIK_DATA:-./data}/runner-state:/var/lib/agentiik" # the runner's key and credential
      # The work root, at the same path on both sides, since the daemon resolves the bind sources
      # of every step's container on this machine. The one path outside AGENTIIK_DATA this file names.
      - /var/lib/agentiik/work:/var/lib/agentiik/work

configs:
  runner-toml:
    content: |
      # false gives up the floor on a daemon that does not remap user namespaces: root in a step's
      # container is then root on this machine. Remap the daemon and set AGENTIIK_REQUIRE_USERNS_REMAP=true.
      require_userns_remap = ${AGENTIIK_REQUIRE_USERNS_REMAP:-false}
  ca:
    # Never empty, since Compose takes a config with no content for a file to bind.
    content: |
      # AGENTIIK_CA: the installation's certificate, which its bus serves, and the proxy's authority
      # where one is in front and the system does not trust it.
      ${AGENTIIK_CA:-}

And its .env, which says what each line is:

runner/.env.example, from agentiik/deploy
# Save as .env beside compose.yaml. AGENTIIK_API is required, AGENTIIK_JOIN_TOKEN and AGENTIIK_CA are
# needed at the first start, and every other line is optional, with the default compose.yaml holds.

# The installation's API, as this machine reaches it: https://AGENTIIK_HOST:8443, or the proxy's URL.
AGENTIIK_API=https://agentiik.example.com:8443

# A join token of the pool this runner joins, which the operator issues, single use and valid an hour.
# Read only where the runner has to join: at the first start, and after AGENTIIK_API or AGENTIIK_LABELS
# changed, which makes it a new runner and takes a new token.
AGENTIIK_JOIN_TOKEN=agkjoin_...

# The certificates the runner trusts beside the system's authorities, in PEM, in double quotes over as
# many lines as it takes: the installation's, which its bus always serves (trust/agentiik.pem, as its
# README copies it), and the proxy's authority where one is in front and the system does not trust it.
AGENTIIK_CA="-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----"

# The labels this runner claims, key=value separated by commas, within what its join token permits.
# Steps whose runs_on names them come here. None is a runner of the pool default.
#AGENTIIK_LABELS=zone=lab

# Where the runner keeps its identity and key: ./data beside compose.yaml, or an absolute path.
#AGENTIIK_DATA=./data

# The version of Agentiik, which is the installation's.
#AGENTIIK_VERSION=v0.2.5

# How many tasks this machine holds at once.
#AGENTIIK_RUNNER_CONCURRENCY=2

# false lets the runner use a Docker daemon that does not remap user namespaces, where root in a
# step's container is root on this machine. true keeps that floor, and needs userns-remap on the daemon.
#AGENTIIK_REQUIRE_USERNS_REMAP=false
on the other machine: download, write the .env, start
$ curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentiik/deploy/v0.2.5/runner/compose.yaml
$ cat > .env <<EOF
AGENTIIK_API=$AGENTIIK_SERVER
AGENTIIK_JOIN_TOKEN=$JOIN_TOKEN
AGENTIIK_LABELS=zone=lab
AGENTIIK_CA="$(cat ./*.pem)"
EOF
$ docker compose up -d

The runner joins at its first start, and restarts with the machine; docker compose logs runner there follows it. Its state is in data/ beside its compose.yaml. The token is read only where the runner has to join: at the first start, and after AGENTIIK_API or AGENTIIK_LABELS changed, which makes it a new runner and takes a new token. The same program runs without a container too, as a static binary under systemd: Installing a runner.

back on the installation's host: a step for the lab
$ mkdir -p ~/on-lab && cd ~/on-lab && git init -q
$ cat > agentiik.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: agentiik.dev/v1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: on-lab
  namespace: demo
steps:
  where:
    image: alpine:3.21
    runs_on: [zone=lab]
    script:
      - echo "where runs on $(hostname)" >&2
    outputs: [out]
EOF
$ git add agentiik.yaml && git commit -qm "A step for the lab"
$ agk push --namespace demo
$ agk run --namespace demo
$ cd ~/agentiik
to remove the machine, there
$ docker compose down
$ sudo rm -rf data /var/lib/agentiik/work

The Mac installation takes no runner from another machine: it listens on the loopback alone.

What v0.2 does not do yet

WhatTodayWhen
Users, groups, sign-inOne operator token may do everything. Only its hash is kept; a new AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN in .env replaces a lost one.v0.3.0 brings principals, and the operator token becomes the bootstrap token that creates the first administrator (First run).
The consoleNot part of either installation. agk is the client.Its own releases.
Creating a namespace through the APIAGENTIIK_NAMESPACE, or docker compose run --rm --no-deps api namespace create team on the installation's host, or agentiik-setup --namespace team on a Mac.v0.3.0: POST /api/v1/namespaces and agk namespace create, by an administrator, with an owner.
Runners on macOS or WindowsRefused: the runner hands the Docker daemon paths on the host to bind, which the virtual machine of Docker Desktop cannot see.
A runner for the Mac installationNone: it listens on the loopback alone, and a runner is a Linux host.
An object storeOn disk, in data/objects, not MinIO or S3.v0.9.0
Purging what has expiredNothing runs the purges or the collection: an expired artifact is refused with 410, but no byte leaves data/objects, and the files of an output given no retain are recorded by nothing.v0.3.0: the controller that leads purges, and the upgrade records what v0.2 left.
network: egressRefused rather than opened.v0.9.0
A certificate from a public authorityinit signs its own, unless a reverse proxy in front serves the API with its own; the bus keeps init's. Yours goes in with docker compose cp to init:/init/api/tls/server.pem and server.key, then docker compose up -d --force-recreate. init keeps it while it names AGENTIIK_HOST, has not expired and is its key's, and never replaces a certificate it did not issue: where yours no longer serves, init refuses to start and says what to do.
§

Use cases

Six workflows, each small enough to read in one sitting and complete enough to push. The services they talk to, Home Assistant, Kubernetes, a bank, appear only at the far end of a script step: Agentiik ships no integration with any of them, and needs none. The scripts a step names sit beside agentiik.yaml in the repository and are not shown.

Use caseStarts onWhat it showsRuns from
Home automationscheduleA runner inside the house, one host per step.v0.9.0
DevOpswebhookA rollout one region at a time, one rollout at a time.v0.9.0
FinancescheduleA join, a human approval, a step never run twice.v0.9.0
CybersecuritywebhookRouting by port, one secret and one host per step.v0.9.0
Data pipelinesagk runCatalog bricks, bad rows on a port of their own.v0.1.0 on your machine, v0.2.0 on a server
AI agent over MCPtools/callA workflow published as a tool.v0.9.0

Most of them reach the network, and that decides the last column: network: egress is refused, not opened, until the proxy enforcing egress.allow lands in v0.9.0 (What does not work yet). A filtered network that is not actually filtered would be worse than waiting.

Home automation

At 22:30, find the windows left open and the doors left unlocked, and send one notification if there are any. Home Assistant is only reachable from inside the house, so the steps run there, on a runner the server never has to reach.

agentiik.yaml, at the root of home/night-check
apiVersion: agentiik.dev/v1
kind: Workflow

metadata:
  name: night-check
  namespace: home

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "30 22 * * *"
      timezone: Europe/Paris

outputs:
  left-open:
    from: { step: find-open, port: open }

secrets: [home-assistant, ntfy]

defaults:
  runs_on: [site=home]              # the runner in the house: it dials out, nothing dials in
  network: egress
  timeout: 2m

steps:
  find-open:
    image: python:3.13-slim
    secrets: [home-assistant]       # a long-lived access token
    egress:
      allow: ["homeassistant.local:8123"]
    retry: { max: 2, on: [failed] }
    script:
      - python /agk/repo/scripts/open_entities.py > /tmp/open.json
      - /agk/bin/agk emit open --from /tmp/open.json --id entity_id
    outputs: [open]

  notify:
    image: curlimages/curl:8.11.1
    needs:
      - { step: find-open, port: open, as: in }
    if: ${{ inputs.in.count > 0 }}  # nothing open, nothing sent
    secrets: [ntfy]
    egress:
      allow: ["ntfy.sh:443"]
    script:
      - 'curl -sSf -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /agk/secrets/ntfy)" -d "$(/agk/bin/agk items | wc -l) left open" https://ntfy.sh/house'
    outputs: [out]
What it usesWhy
scheduleEvery evening in the house's own timezone, with nobody at a keyboard.
runs_onSends both steps to the one pool whose labels include site=home, the only machines that can see homeassistant.local. A runner opens no inbound port, so the house exposes nothing.
secretsEach step mounts its own token as a file under /agk/secrets/, never the other one's.
egressOne host per step: the reader cannot post, the notifier cannot read the house.
agk emitOne item per open entity on the port open, its identity taken from entity_id.
ifinputs.in.count is port metadata: the controller skips the notification without reading a single item.
retryReading states is safe to repeat, and a Wi-Fi hiccup should not cost a night's check.

Available from v0.9.0. The schedule arrives in v0.5.0, and both steps need the egress proxy.

DevOps

Once CI has pushed an image, roll the tag out to three Kubernetes regions, one after another, and say in the team channel how it went. Two tags pushed a minute apart must never interleave.

agentiik.yaml, at the root of platform/deploy-api
apiVersion: agentiik.dev/v1
kind: Workflow

metadata:
  name: deploy-api
  namespace: platform

inputs:
  tag:
    schema: { type: string, pattern: "^v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$" }
    required: true

on:
  webhook:
    - path: /deploy-api        # served at /hooks/platform/deploy-api
      method: POST
      auth: bearer
      response: async
      map:
        tag: ${{ trigger.body.tag }}

concurrency:
  group: deploy-api            # a second tag waits for the first rollout
  cancel_in_progress: false

secrets: [kubeconfig, chat-webhook]

timeout: 1h

steps:
  rollout:
    image: bitnami/kubectl:1.31
    strategy:
      fan_out: matrix
      matrix:
        region: [eu-west, eu-central, us-east]
      max_parallel: 1          # one region at a time
      fail_fast: true          # a failed region stops the rest
    params:
      tag: ${{ workflow.inputs.tag }}
    secrets: [kubeconfig]
    network: egress
    egress:
      allow:
        - k8s.eu-west.example.com:6443
        - k8s.eu-central.example.com:6443
        - k8s.us-east.example.com:6443
    timeout: 15m
    script:
      - export KUBECONFIG=/agk/secrets/kubeconfig
      - kubectl --context "$AGK_PARAM_REGION" -n api set image deployment/api api="registry.example.com/api:$AGK_PARAM_TAG"
      - kubectl --context "$AGK_PARAM_REGION" -n api rollout status deployment/api --timeout=10m
    outputs: [out]

  announce:
    image: curlimages/curl:8.11.1
    needs: [rollout]
    when: [succeeded, failed]  # say so either way
    params:
      tag: ${{ workflow.inputs.tag }}
      outcome: ${{ steps.rollout.status }}
    secrets: [chat-webhook]
    network: egress
    egress:
      allow: ["chat.example.com:443"]
    script:
      - curl -sSf --json "{\"text\":\"api $AGK_PARAM_TAG $AGK_PARAM_OUTCOME\"}" "$(cat /agk/secrets/chat-webhook)"
    outputs: [out]
What it usesWhy
webhookThe last job of the CI pipeline calls it with a bearer token. map turns the body into the tag input, held to its pattern before the run exists.
concurrencyA second tag queues behind the rollout in progress rather than racing it.
matrixOne shard per region. max_parallel: 1 makes it a staged rollout, fail_fast stops it at the first broken region.
paramsThe region and the tag reach the script as AGK_PARAM_REGION and AGK_PARAM_TAG.
whenThe announcement runs on success and on failure; steps.rollout.status says which.
timeoutAn hour for the whole run and fifteen minutes per region, so a stuck rollout never holds the concurrency group for long.
secretsThe kubeconfig is a file for the rollout alone; the chat URL is a secret too, since it is all it takes to post.

Available from v0.9.0. The webhook arrives in v0.5.0, and kubectl reaches the clusters through the egress proxy.

Finance

On the 25th, pay the suppliers whose invoices are due: match each invoice with the supplier's bank details, build one SEPA file, and send it to the bank only once a person has approved it.

agentiik.yaml, at the root of finance/supplier-payments
apiVersion: agentiik.dev/v1
kind: Workflow

metadata:
  name: supplier-payments
  namespace: finance

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 7 25 * *"
      timezone: Europe/Paris

outputs:
  batch:
    from: { step: build-batch, port: out }
    retain: 365d
  unmatched:
    from: { step: build-batch, port: unmatched }

secrets: [accounting, bank]

timeout: 3d                               # three days unapproved: timed_out, never paid late

.accounting:
  image: python:3.13-slim
  secrets: [accounting]
  network: egress
  egress:
    allow: ["accounting.example.com:443"]
  outputs: [out]

steps:
  invoices:
    extends: .accounting
    script:
      - python /agk/repo/scripts/fetch.py invoices > /tmp/invoices.json
      - /agk/bin/agk emit out --from /tmp/invoices.json --id invoice_id

  suppliers:
    extends: .accounting
    script:
      - python /agk/repo/scripts/fetch.py suppliers > /tmp/suppliers.json
      - /agk/bin/agk emit out --from /tmp/suppliers.json --id supplier_id

  build-batch:
    image: python:3.13-slim
    needs:
      - { step: invoices, port: out, as: in }
      - { step: suppliers, port: out, as: in }
    merge:
      join: { on: "$.data.supplier_id" }  # no bank details: leaves by unmatched
    script:
      - python /agk/repo/scripts/sepa.py /agk/out/files/payments.xml
    outputs: [out, unmatched]

  approve:
    image: ghcr.io/agentiik/wait          # the run is waiting until someone approves
    needs: [build-batch]
    outputs: [out]

  pay:
    image: python:3.13-slim
    needs:
      - { step: build-batch, port: out, as: in }
      - { step: approve, port: out, as: approval }
    secrets: [bank]
    network: egress
    egress:
      allow: ["ebics.bank.example.com:443"]
    idempotent: false                     # never sent twice, even after a lost runner
    script:
      - python /agk/repo/scripts/upload.py /agk/in/in/payments.xml
    outputs: [out]
What it usesWhy
merge: joinPairs each invoice with its supplier on supplier_id. An invoice with no bank details leaves by unmatched, a workflow output, instead of failing the batch.
extendsThe two reads from the accounting system share one hidden block.
filesThe SEPA file travels as an artifact with its sha256, and retain: 365d keeps the batch readable for a year.
waitThe run stops in waiting until someone holding workflow:run approves it, from the console, the API or a phone; a rejection ends it cancelled. The wait brick's manifest is v0.8.0 work, so the step passes it no parameters yet and its out port is assumed rather than specified.
idempotent: falseA lost task is never requeued: a payment that may have left is handed to a person, not sent again.
timeoutThree days without an approval end the run timed_out, rather than paying a week late.

Available from v0.9.0. The schedule arrives in v0.5.0, the wait step and its approval in v0.8.0, and the accounting system and the bank are reached through the egress proxy.

Cybersecurity

When the SIEM raises an alert, score its source address against a threat-intelligence service and block it at the firewall if it is hostile. The alert is written by the attacker as much as by the SIEM, so each step gets as little as it can work with.

agentiik.yaml, at the root of soc/ip-triage
apiVersion: agentiik.dev/v1
kind: Workflow

metadata:
  name: ip-triage
  namespace: soc

inputs:
  alert:
    schema:
      type: object
      required: [rule, src_ip]
      properties:
        rule: { type: string }
        src_ip: { type: string, format: ipv4 }
    required: true

on:
  webhook:
    - path: /siem-alert
      method: POST
      auth: hmac
      response: async
      map:
        alert: ${{ trigger.body }}

outputs:
  blocked:
    from: { step: block, port: out }
    retain: 30d
  dismissed:
    from: { step: score, port: benign }

secrets: [abuseipdb, firewall]

steps:
  score:
    image: python:3.13-slim
    inputs:
      in: ${{ workflow.inputs.alert }}
    secrets: [abuseipdb]                # this step's one secret
    network: egress
    egress:
      allow: ["api.abuseipdb.com:443"]  # and its one host
    retry: { max: 3, on: [transient] }  # score.py exits 100 on a 429 or a 5xx
    script:
      - python /agk/repo/scripts/score.py > /tmp/verdict.json
      - /agk/bin/agk emit hostile --from /tmp/verdict.json --filter '.hostile'
      - /agk/bin/agk emit benign --from /tmp/verdict.json --filter '.hostile | not'
    outputs: [hostile, benign]

  block:
    image: python:3.13-slim
    needs:
      - { step: score, port: hostile, as: in }
    if: ${{ inputs.in.count > 0 }}
    secrets: [firewall]
    network: egress
    egress:
      allow: ["firewall.soc.example.com:443"]
    script:
      - python /agk/repo/scripts/block.py
    outputs: [out]
What it usesWhy
auth: hmacThe SIEM signs each alert, and a body that does not verify starts nothing.
inputsThe alert is held to its schema before a run exists: one without src_ip never reaches a container.
portsscore decides by publishing on hostile or benign, and the graph routes by port. No expression reads the alert (why).
secrets and egressOne secret and one host per step. A parsing bug in score gives away a threat-intelligence key, not the firewall.
retry on transientA rate limit is exit code 100 and is retried; a malformed answer exits 1 and is not.
retainWhat was blocked stays readable for thirty days, long enough to write the incident up.

Available from v0.9.0. The webhook and its signature check arrive in v0.5.0, and both calls go through the egress proxy.

Data pipelines

Each month, three shops drop a CSV export into the repository. Turn them into rows, hold every row to a schema, total the good ones per shop, and hand back a table, without one malformed line sinking the month.

agentiik.yaml, at the root of data/monthly-sales
apiVersion: agentiik.dev/v1
kind: Workflow

metadata:
  name: monthly-sales
  namespace: data

outputs:
  totals:
    from: { step: report, port: out }
  rejected:
    from: { step: check, port: invalid }

steps:
  exports:
    image: alpine:3.21
    strategy:
      fan_out: matrix
      matrix:
        shop: [paris, lyon, lille]  # one shard per shop
    script:
      - cp "/agk/repo/exports/$AGK_PARAM_SHOP.csv" /agk/out/files/
    outputs: [out]

  rows:
    image: ghcr.io/agentiik/csv:0.1.0
    needs: [exports]
    params: { direction: to_items }
    outputs: [out]

  check:
    image: ghcr.io/agentiik/schema-validate:0.1.0
    needs: [rows]
    params: { schema_path: schemas/sale.json }
    outputs: [ok, invalid]          # a bad row leaves by invalid

  totals:
    image: python:3.13-slim
    needs:
      - { step: check, port: ok, as: in }
    script:
      - python /agk/repo/scripts/totals.py > /tmp/totals.json
      - /agk/bin/agk emit out --from /tmp/totals.json --id shop
    outputs: [out]

  report:
    image: ghcr.io/agentiik/csv:0.1.0
    needs: [totals]
    params: { direction: to_table, table_name: totals.csv }
    outputs: [out]
What it usesWhy
matrixOne shard per shop, each copying its own export.
a file in /agk/out/files/A script that writes no port publishes one item, with the file attached: no helper needed.
csv, schema-validateParsing and validation are deterministic tools from the catalog, not code to write.
portsA bad row leaves by invalid with its violations, straight to the workflow output rejected, and the month still totals.
artifactsA table larger than inline_max_bytes travels as an artifact rather than inline.
network: noneThe default, and nothing here needs more: no step can leave the machine.

Available from v0.1.0 with agk run --local, and from v0.2.0 on a server with agk push and agk run --namespace, since no step reaches the network. The two bricks are built from agentiik/bricks until the catalog is published to ghcr.io/agentiik in v0.8.0.

AI agent over MCP

A support assistant needs to answer "where is my order?" without holding the orders service's credentials or being able to reach it. The workflow is the boundary: the model calls one tool, and the step behind it holds the key.

agentiik.yaml, at the root of support/order-status
apiVersion: agentiik.dev/v1
kind: Workflow

metadata:
  name: order-status
  namespace: support

inputs:
  query:
    schema:
      type: object
      required: [order_id]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        order_id: { type: string, pattern: "^ORD-[0-9]{6}$" }
    required: true

outputs:
  status:
    from: { step: lookup, port: out }
    schema:
      type: object
      required: [order_id, state]
      properties:
        order_id: { type: string }
        state: { enum: [paid, shipped, delivered, refunded] }
        tracking_url: { type: string }

mcp:
  name: orders
  description: Customer orders, read-only.
  tools:
    - name: order_status
      title: Order status
      description: Return the state of one order and, once shipped, its tracking link. Takes an order number such as ORD-004211 and nothing else.
      input: { from: { input: query } }
      output: { from: { output: status } }
      mode: sync
      timeout: 30s
      annotations:
        readOnlyHint: true
        idempotentHint: true

secrets: [orders-api]

steps:
  lookup:
    image: python:3.13-slim
    inputs:
      in: ${{ workflow.inputs.query }}
    secrets: [orders-api]  # the model never holds it
    network: egress
    egress:
      allow: ["orders.internal.example.com:443"]
    timeout: 20s
    script:
      - python /agk/repo/scripts/lookup.py > /tmp/status.json
      - /agk/bin/agk emit out --from /tmp/status.json --id order_id
    outputs: [out]
What it usesWhy
mcpOne tool, order_status, whose inputSchema is the query input's schema as it stands and whose result is the status output.
/mcp/support/order-statusThe workflow is an MCP server of its own, listed and called with workflow:run alone, which reaches no step, no file and no endpoint behind it.
operatorThe role to grant the assistant's service account: it runs the tool and follows its runs, and reads neither the workflow nor their data.
input validationAn argument that does not match ^ORD-[0-9]{6}$ is refused as a protocol error before any run is created.
mode: syncThe answer comes back in the call, within the tool's 30 seconds.
