A line's id is task_id/seq/line and a dispatch's task_id/0/0, which Last-Event-ID resumes from; dispatch_end and end carry none. A client closes on end. A comment every 15 s keeps it alive; X-Accel-Buffering: no. 400 for an id the stream never gave, 404 for a step the run does not have, 410 past retention. Requires run:read. See Observability.
GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/outputs/{name}One workflow output's envelope. Requires run:read_data. 404 while the run records no output of that name (it has not ended, or declares none); 410 once its envelope was purged.
GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/steps/{step}/outputs/{port}One step's output envelope on a port. Requires run:read_data. 404 while the step has published nothing there; 410 once its envelope was purged.
GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/steps/{step}/inputs/{port}?attempt=&shard=What a dispatch of the step was handed on an input port, under /agk/in/. attempt counts from 1 as AGK_ATTEMPT does, the last by default; shard is AGK_SHARD, required where the step fans out. Requires run:read_data. 400 for a missing or malformed attempt or shard, 404 for a dispatch or port not there, 410 once purged.
GET /api/v1/artifacts/{uri}302 to a short-lived presigned URL, or the bytes themselves where the artifact has a fetch budget, since a redirect cannot be counted. Requires run:read_data.
POST /hooks/{ns}/{path}Webhook triggers.
Statistics, from v0.6.0
GET /api/v1/{ns}/stats/runsPer bucket, the runs of the namespace's workflows by final state, the p50, p95 and p99 of their duration and of their tasks' queue wait, and the attempts retried by exit code; with histogram=N, their durations over the range in N bins. Narrowed by workflow. Counts only the workflows the caller holds run:read on, as GET /api/v1/runs lists them (Statistics).
GET /api/v1/{ns}/stats/stepsPer step of a workflow, per bucket: the percentiles of its duration, its attempts and exit codes, and a fan-out's items a minute; with by=hour, its p50 by weekday and hour over the range. Requires run:read on the workflow.
GET /api/v1/{ns}/stats/portsPer port of each step of a workflow, per bucket, the items published and the share rejected or sent to error, from each envelope's meta.count and never its items. Requires run:read on the workflow, and never run:read_data.
GET /api/v1/{ns}/stats/quotasPer bucket, the runs created and those refused with 429, the most tasks in flight at once, and the artifact bytes live, each beside the quota it meets. Read by whoever reads the namespace.
GET /api/v1/stats/poolsPer pool and per runner, per bucket: the slots in use and the capacity, and each silence between heartbeats of 20 s or more, with its length and the tasks it cost. Administrator only.

Every statistics route takes from and to (RFC 3339, the last 24 hours when left out), bucket (1m, 15m, 1h or 1d, chosen from the range when left out, and refused with 400 past 1,000 buckets) and compare=previous, which adds the same span before the range. It answers JSON, or CSV to Accept: text/csv, and every bucket carries the since and until that GET /api/v1/runs takes, so that a point opens the runs it counts.

a manual trigger
> POST /api/v1/finance/workflows/monthly-invoicing/runs
Authorization: Bearer <api token>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "commit": "3f9c2e1d…", "inputs": { "orders": [ … ] } }

A workflow the caller cannot see answers the same 404 as an absent one, and so does a run of such a workflow.

Starting a run answersWhen
202The run is queued, with Location naming it.
400A body refused as Request bodies below says, or no commit.
404No such version, or a workflow the caller holds no workflow:run on.
413As below.
422{error, input, rule}, rule being required, schema or undeclared; or a declaration that does not compile, which only a version pushed before pushes checked it can hold.
429From v0.3.0, the namespace has created max_runs_per_hour runs in the last 60 minutes. Retry-After gives the whole seconds until one more fits, and the error names the quota. Asked last, once the inputs are bound, so a request refused for anything else counts nothing. No run is written and nothing is audited: the audit log records acts, and one entry per refused request would let whoever floods the route lengthen the chain.
500The version or its tree could not be read.
503A schema names a file of the tree and the installation has no object store attached.
A cancellation answersWhen
202The request is written: {"run": …}, and Location: /api/v1/{ns}/runs/{id}, where the run is read. The same whether the run is going or has ended, since how it stands is for run:read to show, and cancelling takes workflow:run alone.
400A body with a field in it, or one that is not a JSON object.
404No such run, or a run whose workflow the caller holds no workflow:run on.
413A body past 64 KiB.
Cancelling a runWhat happens
the requestThe API writes the moment on the run, keeping the first if asked again, and notifies the controller. It stops nothing itself: the two share the database and nothing else.
the controller's next passBefore admission, so a queued run is never let in to be called off. The run ends cancelled; one that never left the queue has no started_at.
its tasksEvery task not over is written cancelled in that pass, so a message still on the queue redeems nothing and the run's share of max_concurrent_tasks comes back at once. The runners holding redeemed ones are asked to stop them on the bus subject agentiik.stops, which every runner subscribes to over its own connection, so a stop arrives at once and nothing connects to a runner. It is not kept, so the heartbeat's answer repeats it as cancel to a runner that missed it. A lost dispatch keeps its loss. The stopped runner's report arrives after the run has ended and changes nothing but the task's exit code, log and usage, which it adds to the row once.
the audit logRecords the request in the transaction that writes it, and any request after the first, or about a run already over, as unchanged.

Request bodies

BodyAt mostCounted
a pool, a join token, the join, a redemption, a bus credential, a cancellation, a namespace, its quotas, an API token, a user, a group, a grant, a service account, and every route that reads no body64 KiB1,024 labels, namespaces, pools, permissions or places a token's scope names, or first members of a group
a heartbeat1 MiB4,096 keys
a log shipment1 MiB4,096 lines
starting a run4 MiB100,000 values in the inputs, at any depth. Both bounds are an envelope's, at the size rules' defaults.
a push16 MiB4,096 includes or manifests, and the tree's own limits
a secret's PUT2 MiBa value of 1 MiB (Secrets)
a form posted to /objects/{ns}64 KiB before the filethe file, up to artifact_max_bytes
RefusedWith
a body past its size, a list or the inputs past their count, or the inputs with the defaults the workflow declares past 100,000 values or 4 MiB as written413
a form posted to /objects/{ns} carrying more than 64 KiB before its file400 with no body, as every refusal of the store; its 413 is for a file past artifact_max_bytes, and its 507 for one its namespace's max_artifact_bytes leaves no room for
a field the route does not read, a field or a path written twice, text that is not UTF-8, anything after the document400
a body sent to a route that reads none, such as a removal, beyond {}400, or 413 past 64 KiB
null for a namespace's kind, its quotas or one quota, or as the whole body of a quotas PUT400, since read as left out it would lift a bound, or keep one, that a client meant to set
an empty principal or device_label in a token's request, or a label over 256 characters400: leaving the field out is how a token of one's own, or one with no label, is asked for
in a run's inputs: U+0000 in a string or a name, a number no 64-bit float holds or holds only as zero, or one written past 340 digits from the point400
a body that is not JSON400, saying where it stops being JSON and never repeating the bytes there, which may be part of a secret
A log shipment is refusedWith
a malformed chunk, or a grant in the body400
no grant, a grant that opens nothing, a key differing from the grant's401
a task not this runner's, a run past its retention, the same seq with other lines, a first_line not where the log ended, a chunk after the last one409

A run's inputs are counted as they are read, then bound against the version's declaration by the same code agk run --local binds with: required and default applied, each value held to its schema as it was written, so 2^53 + 1 is past a maximum of 2^53, an undeclared name refused. The run records what was bound, defaults included, each number as it was written save an exponent, written out with a point (1e3 as 1000.0) so that it reads back a double.

Decision

A cap per route, rather than one that fits the largest body, and every list counted as it is read: decoding costs values more than bytes, and 8 MiB of inputs written [{},{},...] once cost 508 MiB to read. Read a token at a time, a body now costs at most two and a half times its cap, and it is held as it arrives, not as it declares.

Command line

InstallGives
brew trust agentiik/tapOnce, before either formula: Homebrew loads the formulae of a third-party tap only once that tap is trusted.
brew install agentiik/tap/agkagk, built from the tagged source, with the static helper embedded for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.
brew install agentiik/tap/agentiikagentiik-api, agentiik-controller and agk-runner, with agk, built from the tagged source, or from main with --HEAD. PostgreSQL and NATS are not pulled in: the formula's caveats say how to run both on one host.
go install github.com/agentiik/agentiik/cmd/agk@<tag>agk without the embedded helper; --helper or $AGK_HELPER supplies one.
CommandEffect
agk loginSigns in against an installation in the browser, with a passkey or a password where the policy allows one, through a loopback redirect and a one-time code (Authentication), and stores an API token in the local profile, revoking the one it kept for that installation before. --label names the token, agk on and the machine's name by default. Over SSH, or with no display, it prints the page's address and the port to forward instead of opening a browser. It waits 5 minutes, and says who it signed in as.
agk logoutRevokes the token agk login stored for an installation, presenting it, and removes it from the local profile. A token the installation no longer accepts is removed all the same; one whose revocation cannot be told, the installation not answering or answering 5xx, is kept for agk logout to revoke later. With nothing kept, it has nothing to do and succeeds.
agk token createMints an API token for you, or with --for NS/NAME for a service account of a namespace you own, and prints the token alone on standard output, this once, saying on standard error what it minted: TOKEN=$(agk token create --for finance/nightly-sync --expires 30d --scope workflow:run --scope finance/monthly-invoicing --label ci). --expires takes days, a duration or an RFC 3339 instant; a --scope entry holding a colon is a permission kept, any other a namespace or workflow reached.
agk token listLists the tokens you may revoke that are still accepted, newest first: identifier, principal, expiry, last use, scope and label.
agk token revokeRevokes one token, by the identifier agk token list prints, from its next request.
agk whoamiPrints the current principal, whether an administrator, its groups, and its effective permissions at every scope where it holds any, or on the namespace or workflow named, agk whoami finance/monthly-invoicing; with none named, the notifications the installation tells it, each by the identifier that dismisses it. -o json writes GET /api/v1/me's answer.
agk user createCreates a user, --admin for an administrator, --display-name for the name people read, the login where it is left out, and prints the enrolment link. Run again for a user who has not enrolled, it prints a fresh link, what it leaves out keeping what is recorded. The first administrator is created this way with the bootstrap token (First run).
agk user recoverIssues a user a recovery code and prints the link that carries it, once, for you to hand over: an administrator's to run for somebody else, never for themselves (Authentication).
agk user listLists the users: login, display name, and whether an administrator or suspended.
agk user showShows one user: display name, whether an administrator or suspended, when created and last signed in.
agk user deleteRemoves a user with what they hold, and their personal namespace where it is empty.
agk group createCreates a group, empty or with its first members: agk group create team-finance alice bob.
agk group listLists the groups and their members.
agk group showShows one group and its members.
agk group deleteRemoves a group with its memberships and grants; its members stay.
agk group add
agk group remove		Puts a user in a group, or takes them out, touching no grant: agk group add team-finance carol. Every agk user and agk group verb is an administrator's, and the reads take -o json.
agk service-account createCreates a service account, NS/NAME, in a namespace you own, holding no grant and no token: agk service-account create finance/nightly-sync, then agk token create --for finance/nightly-sync.
agk service-account listLists the service accounts of the namespaces you own, or of the one named, the built-in identity of each among them, with who created each and when.
agk service-account deleteRemoves a service account with its tokens and grants.
agk auth policyPrints the authentication policy, of the installation or of --namespace, and with settings given, --password, --passkey, --user-verification, --device-bound-only and --min-passkeys, reads it, sets them on top and sends the whole of it, so a setting nobody named is kept. --inherit min_passkeys drops one of a namespace's settings, which it then inherits from the installation's, repeated for each; -o json writes the answer (Authentication).
agk namespace createCreates a shared namespace: agk namespace create finance --owner group:team-finance --max-runs-per-hour 500 --allowed-runner-pools default,dmz. --owner is required; each quota is a flag named after it with hyphens. Administrator only.
agk namespace listLists the namespaces the caller holds a grant in, every one for an administrator: name, kind and owner.
agk namespace showShows one namespace: its kind, its owner and the quotas it sets.
agk namespace deleteRemoves a namespace that holds nothing but its built-in identity. Administrator only.
agk namespace quotasPrints a namespace's quotas. With quotas given, it reads them first, sets those given on top and sends the whole set, so a bound nobody named is kept: the route replaces the whole set, and a person typing one flag means one bound, not the others lifted with it, allowed_runner_pools among them. --lift max_runs_per_hour lifts one, repeated for each; max_concurrent_tasks and max_retention_days always hold a value and are set, never lifted. Administrator only to change.
agk validateValidates the YAML, resolves includes and inheritance, detects cycles, checks ports against the manifests of the referenced images.
agk graphWrites the resolved graph as DOT or Mermaid, for review inside a merge request.
agk run --localRuns the whole workflow against the local Docker daemon, with no controller, no bus and no database. Artifacts land in a working directory.
agk run --namespaceStarts a run of a pushed commit on an installation and follows it until it ends, narrated and reported as a local run is. --commit names the commit, HEAD by default. Its inputs are sent as given and the installation binds them against the commit's declaration; a refusal is the sentence a local run prints, and a run refused when it is let in ends with its reason, exit 3. An interrupt stops the following, never the run (Pointing agk at an installation).
agk pushRegisters the workflow in a namespace on a server, each image resolved to its registry digest (Supply chain). Until git hosting, it carries the committed tree itself, as set out here.
agk shareGrants or revokes access to a namespace or a workflow: agk share finance/monthly-invoicing --group team-ops --role operator. --user, --group or --service-account NS/NAME names the principal, --deny PERMISSION takes one permission away in place of a role, and --expires takes days, a duration or an RFC 3339 instant. agk share finance --revoke ID revokes one written there, by the identifier agk grants prints.
agk grantsShows the grants and denies on a namespace or a workflow, one a line: identifier, principal, role or deny, the scope it was written at, which tells a workflow's own from what it inherits, the permissions a role gives there, and the expiry.
agk logsFollows the logs of a run, or of the steps named after it, history then live, each line behind its step, shard and attempt. A stream cut off, or silent past three keep-alives, is asked again from its last event, and nothing is printed twice.
agk statusShows how a run on an installation stands: its state, each step's verdict with the digest of each port, its inputs where run:read_data allows, its outputs and what failed, or the reason a run refused when it was let in carries. -o json writes the API's answer.
agk consoleOpens the console in the terminal, full screen, over the routes the web console reads: runs, a run with its log, its graph, workflows, sharing and, for an administrator, runners. Not on a terminal, it prints the view once as plain lines (Terminal console).
agk brick initScaffolds a brick in a chosen language, with its manifest and test harness.
agk brick testRuns the brick against a set of sample envelopes and compares against expected outputs.

The programs of an installation are not agk. Each reads its settings as Configuration lists them.

ProgramEffect
agk-runner joinTrades a join token for a runner's identity: --api, --token and, where it claims labels, --labels, or AGK_API and AGK_RUNNER_LABELS. Without either it claims none, as a runner of the pool default does. Run as root, it writes the key and /etc/agentiik/runner.env and gives both to --user, agentiik by default. --replace makes a host that has joined a new runner (Registering a runner).
agk-runner serveThe agent: heartbeats, pulls, runs, publishes. What the systemd unit and the container run. Given a join token in AGK_RUNNER_JOIN_TOKEN or AGK_RUNNER_JOIN_TOKEN_FILE, it joins on its own where it has to (Registering a runner). Started as root, it drops to agentiik before it serves.
agk-runner versionPrints the agent version join sends.
agentiik-api serveServes every route, the built-in object store and the secret providers, and makes every runner pool's queue ready as it starts, refusing to start where the bus refuses one. At SIGTERM it finishes the requests being answered for up to 30 s, and a second signal ends it. Without a verb the program exits 2.
agentiik-api initPrepares an installation in AGK_INIT_DIR, one subdirectory per service, and brings it in line with its settings at every run: the certificate for AGK_INIT_HOST, marked O=agentiik-api init and replaced only where init issued it; the master key, the presign key, the database password and the bus identity, made once and kept; the migration; the namespace AGK_INIT_NAMESPACE, or a line saying a login holds its name; from v0.3.0 the built-in identity of every namespace made before it; a fresh one-hour join token of the pool default for the runner beside it; from v0.3.0 the artifact files of the runs v0.2 finished, read from their envelopes in objects and recorded each expiring its namespace's max_retention_days after its run finished, leaving what it cannot record to the controller rather than failing; and the operator token's hash, last, into the database from v0.3.0. Prints the certificate at every run. A certificate a person put there that no longer names the host, has expired or is not its key's refuses the start, saying what to do.
agentiik-api migrateApplies the migrations as a privileged role, and creates the NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role the API and the controller connect as. From v0.3.0 it then gives every namespace made before it its built-in identity, as init does, and keeps the bootstrap token's hash as init does, signed in as that role, for Homebrew's server and one built by hand, which run it at every start: AGK_OPERATOR_TOKEN set replaces the hash, and with none set and none kept it imports the v0.2 hash from the file AGK_OPERATOR_TOKEN_FILE names, once. It also records the artifact files of the runs v0.2 finished, as init does, where AGK_OBJECTS_DIR is set, which it reads and never writes; unset, it records none and says so, and the controller that leads records them (Configuration).
agentiik-api namespace create NAMECreates a namespace with no owner, for an installation script and for init, which create one before anybody could ask the API; from v0.3.0 an administrator uses POST /api/v1/namespaces, and the namespace comes with its built-in NAME/agentiik either way. Lowercase words joined by hyphens, at most 255 characters, none of the reserved words, as the API holds a name. Creating one that exists changes nothing and says so, so that a script run twice succeeds twice. Reads AGK_DATABASE_URL and AGK_DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE, so it runs where the API runs, and records namespace.create by installation.
agentiik-api namespace remove NAMERemoves a namespace that holds no workflow, run, secret, stored object or service account but its built-in identity, which goes first, and refuses one that does, saying what it holds, as DELETE /api/v1/namespaces/{ns} does; a user's personal namespace is refused too. Records namespace.delete by installation.
agentiik-api recover LOGINThe break-glass line of recovery, for the day no administrator can sign in: issues the administrator LOGIN a recovery code and prints the link that carries it, once, for whoever runs it to hand over. It takes no credential, and runs where the API runs, with its settings, docker compose run --rm --no-deps api recover alice in the Compose installation, so that the network brings nobody to it. Recorded as enrolment.issue by installation, and told to every administrator in GET /api/v1/me. Refuses a login no user holds and a user who is not an administrator, who is recovered with agk user recover.
agentiik-api bus-init DIRCreates the installation's NATS operator and accounts, once, and writes accounts.conf, account.seed and control-plane.creds in DIR, each mode 0600, the credential valid 90 days. Refuses a DIR its group or anybody else may write to. See Configuration.
agentiik-api bus-credential DIRMints a new 90-day control-plane.creds in DIR from the account seed, leaving the operator and the accounts alone. agentiik-api init moves it to the bus directory, where the API renews it itself. The API and the controller reread the file at every connection to the bus, so they take it with no restart when the bus drops the credential it replaces, at that one's expiry; a restart takes it at once.
agentiik-api healthExits 0 once the API serving in the same container answers, and 1 saying why otherwise: the Compose file's health check, run in the exec form since the image has no shell. It asks where AGK_LISTEN says serve listens, on the loopback where that is every interface, in plain HTTP behind AGK_PROXY_URL and over TLS without verifying otherwise, never through a proxy, for up to 5 s. Any answer counts as ready, since serve answers nothing until the database, the bus and every route are open.
agentiik-api audit-verify FILEChecks the chain of an audit log export, one entry per line, repeats allowed, and prints how far it holds or where it breaks, exiting 1. Reads no environment and no database (Audit log).
agentiik-controllerLeads by advisory lock, sweeps, consumes results and publishes tasks, and from v0.3.0 runs the purges, the collection and the orphan sweep while it leads (What each purge acts on).
Decision

Joining is a verb of agk-runner, not of agk: join writes what serve reads, so a runner host needs one binary, and agk links the API and through it the database and the controller, which the agent must keep out and a boundary test of its own will hold, as driver and graph have theirs. The API and the controller are two programs rather than one because only the API may link the secret store.

Decision

agk run --local is an architectural constraint, not a convenience: the graph evaluator and the container driver must work as libraries without a bus or a database, so no execution rule can hide in the controller, where the YAML file cannot show it. Local runs bypass grants entirely because there is nothing to protect: the operator already owns the file, the daemon and the secrets they supply on the command line.

A local run, from the file to the envelopes

A recording, not a hand-written transcript: a fan-out over three orders, a merge waiting for both its edges, a script step reading items through the helper. Six containers, 2.2 seconds. agk-local-run.cast replays it with asciinema play.

finance/monthly-invoicing, on a laptop
$ agk validate
user namespace remapping is off on this daemon and this runner does not require it, so the floor is lifted: a task's files are owned by a real uid on the host, root inside a container is the host's own root, and a process that escapes a container is that account rather than an unprivileged high-numbered one that maps to no real user.
this daemon applies neither an AppArmor profile nor an SELinux label to a container, which is the host's to offer, so a container is held by its namespaces, its dropped capabilities and its seccomp profile with no mandatory access control behind them.

FlagEffect
--inputs file.jsonA JSON object of the workflow's declared inputs.
--input name=value
--input-file name=path		One input at a time.
--secret name=value
--secret-file name=path		Where a local run's secrets come from. A step mounting a secret nobody supplied is refused before any container exists, not at the fourth shard of a fan-out.
-o jsonOutput envelopes on standard output, one object keyed by output name, to compose with whatever reads next. Narration stays on standard error.
--logsPrints what each container wrote.
-vNarrates every task, not only every step: one line per shard.
--dirMoves the working directory.
--helperThe static /agk/bin/agk to mount, or none to mount nothing.
--require-userns-remapRefuses a daemon without user-namespace remapping, the floor every server runner holds. Off by default for a local run, because Docker Desktop does not offer the remapping.

What a local run leaves behind

Everything, under .agk beside the entry point, because at three in the morning finding it matters more than tidiness.

.agk
objects/<namespace>/sha256/<digest>   # the artifact store: content addressed, shared by every run
bin/agk-linux-arm64                   # the static helper, laid down once, bound read-only
runs/<run>/run.json                   # the run: workflow, commit, state, timings
runs/<run>/state.json                 # every step and every task, as the evaluator left it
runs/<run>/outputs/<output>.json      # one envelope per declared output
runs/<run>/logs/<step>/               # what each container wrote, masked
  • Under runs/<run>/logs/<step>/, standard output is kept beside standard error up to envelope_max_bytes and log_max_lines, counted apart, with a line of the driver's where it stops.
  • A task's own working directory is created outside this tree and removed with the container, because the tree is bound read-only into every container and no task may read another's directory through it.
  • A run carries a ULID and is labelled local, so a history that later holds server runs cannot mistake one for the other.

Pointing agk at an installation

A first run on a server, step by step: Get started. Trusting the certificate of an installation from another machine: Install a server.

SettingIs
--server
AGENTIIK_SERVER		The installation: https, or http to a loopback address alone, since every request carries the token. No redirect is followed.
AGENTIIK_TOKENThe API token: the interim operator's until v0.3.0, then the bootstrap token until it ends, and after that a service account's for a script, where a person uses agk login. Never a flag: an argument is in the shell history, the process list and whatever recorded the terminal. Where it is not set, agk presents the token agk login stored for the installation --server or AGENTIIK_SERVER names; set, it wins.
the local profileagentiik/profile.json under the user's configuration directory: ~/.config/agentiik on Linux, where XDG_CONFIG_HOME moves it, and ~/Library/Application Support/agentiik on macOS. One token per installation address, written by agk login 0600 in a directory 0700, whole and then renamed, and read only while nobody but its owner may read or write it, since one others may read is a token already leaked and one they may write a token somebody else chose. A machine with no configuration directory keeps none.
agk run on a serverEffect
--namespaceThe namespace the workflow was pushed to. Its presence is what makes the run a server's.
--commit <hash|branch|tag>A commit the repository holds, pushed as a version. HEAD by default.
--input, --input-file, --inputs, -o json, -vAs for a local run.
--secret, --secret-file, --dir, --helper, --require-userns-remap, --logsRefused: the namespace declares the secrets, the runner holds the rest, and agk logs follows the logs.
Decision

An interrupt stops following a server run and not the run: the run is the installation's, others may be reading it, and cancelling is POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/cancel, under workflow:run.

The graph, for a merge request

The resolved graph, not the file's text: includes resolved, inheritance applied, ports named as the manifests declare them. Mermaid renders inside a merge request; --format dot writes a digraph.

agk graph --format mermaid
$ agk graph --format mermaid
flowchart LR
	step_archive["archive<br/>script on alpine:3.21"]
	step_charge["charge<br/>ghcr.io/acme/agk-charge:0.1.0<br/>fan_out: item"]
	step_split["split<br/>ghcr.io/acme/agk-split:0.1.0"]
	step_total["total<br/>ghcr.io/acme/agk-total:0.1.0<br/>merge: wait_all"]

	step_total -->|"ok to in"| step_archive
	step_split -->|"ok to in"| step_charge
	step_charge -->|"ok to charges"| step_total
	step_charge -->|"rejected to charges"| step_total

	input_orders(["orders"])
	input_orders -. "orders" .-> step_split
	output_archived(["archived"])
	step_archive -. "out" .-> output_archived
	output_charged(["charged"])
	step_charge -. "ok" .-> output_charged
	output_invoiced(["invoiced"])
	step_total -. "ok" .-> output_invoiced
	output_rejected(["rejected"])
	step_charge -. "rejected" .-> output_rejected

The exit codes of agk

They tell a script around agk what to do next. A brick's exit code is another thing, read against its own table.

CodeMeaning
0The command did what it says, and a run reached succeeded.
1Refused, and nothing ran: the workflow was refused, an input was refused, a secret a step mounts was not supplied, a brick test case did not match, or an installation refused the run with 429 for max_runs_per_hour, since no run was written; agk login's sign-in did not come back within 5 minutes, came back with no code agk can use, or was interrupted, its exchange was refused, or the token it minted could not be kept and was revoked; or agk logout's revocation was refused, the token kept.
2The command line was wrong, or what it needs around it is missing: no credential, a local profile agk cannot use (not a file, readable or writable by others than its owner, not read, not writable), or a token kept past its expiry.
3The run reached a terminal state other than succeeded. It ran, and it did not succeed.
4No outcome could be determined: the daemon could not be reached, the floor refused, a pull died, a working directory could not be prepared, an installation stopped answering, a run on one stopped being followed before it ended, or a change was answered with a 5xx, after which it may have been made: a namespace, a user or a group, a grant, a service account, or a token minted or revoked, which reading it back tells. A read of users, groups, grants or agk whoami answered with a 5xx is 4 too, since it may answer if asked again; agk service-account list answered so is 1. So is agk login unable to listen on the loopback, its exchange unanswered or answered with a 5xx, or a token it minted neither kept nor revoked; and agk logout's revocation unanswered or answered with a 5xx, or its profile not rewritten after it: agk token list shows what is live.
Decision

3 and 4 are separate because the next move differs. A failed run is a run to look at: the narration names the step, the exit code and its band. No outcome is a machine to look at. It is the driver's split between a result and an error, carried to the shell, so a broken daemon never reads as a broken workflow.

§

Native MCP

Agentiik speaks the Model Context Protocol on two surfaces: /mcp operates the platform, and /mcp/{namespace}/{workflow} presents one workflow as a tool.

Decision

MCP puts no model in the engine. Both surfaces are servers: Agentiik publishes tools and answers calls, and any model lives in the client, beyond a protocol boundary the engine never crosses. The rule in Scope holds unchanged: no language-model node and no agent, in the engine or in the standard catalog.

Protocol

AspectRule
revision2026-07-28, declared by every request in _meta under io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion and, on HTTP, in the MCP-Protocol-Version header. server/discover is implemented because the specification requires it.
transportStreamable HTTP, one endpoint, POST and GET. Origin is validated on every connection, as the transport requires. Mcp-Session-Id is issued at initialisation.
authorisationOAuth 2.1, Agentiik as resource server. It publishes Protected Resource Metadata, accepts only a token issued for it as the audience, and never forwards a token issued for anything else. Invalid token: 401. Missing scope: 403 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope".
API tokenAn ordinary API bearer token is also accepted, so a service account needs no browser.
instructionsOrientation in the discovery response: a workflow is a git repository, the entry point is agentiik.yaml at its root, workflow.language comes before drafting and workflow.validate before committing. That is the field's purpose in the specification, "natural-language guidance for LLMs on how to use this server effectively", and it carries nothing else.

The platform server

At /mcp. Its tools mirror the API and hold no authority of their own: each call runs as the presenting principal, under the grants that govern the console.

ToolWhat it doesNeeds
workflow.listWorkflows in namespaces the caller can see.workflow:read
workflow.getEntry point and resolved graph at a ref.workflow:read
workflow.languageThe language, one topic at a time, with examples.any authenticated principal
workflow.schemaJSON Schema 2020-12 of the entry point, a brick manifest or an envelope, for local validation or type generation.any authenticated principal
workflow.validateValidates a draft entry point and file set, committing nothing. The only authority on whether a draft is legal.workflow:read
workflow.createEmpty repository with its default branch.namespace owner
workflow.commitWrites files and commits to a branch, through the pre-receive validation.workflow:write, and secret:use where the commit names a secret
workflow.runStarts a run, optionally on a ref other than the default branch.workflow:run
run.list, run.getRun history and state; without run:read_data, a run names no inputs.run:read
run.logsA step's log tail, secrets masked.run:read
run.outputA named output of a finished run.run:read_data
run.cancel, run.replayAct on a run in flight.workflow:run
run.approve, run.rejectAct on a waiting run. With the wait step, in v0.8.0.workflow:run
brick.list, brick.getThe catalog; a manifest with its parameter schema.any authenticated principal
runner.listRunner inventory.administrator

Resources are read-only:

ResourceIs
agentiik://{ns}/{name}/tree/{ref}/{path}A file in a workflow repository.
agentiik://run/{id}A run.
agentiik://brick/{name}A brick manifest.
agentiik://schema/{part}A schema document.
agentiik://language/{topic}A page of the language reference, for clients that prefer attaching documents to calling workflow.language.
Decision

The tool list is filtered by the caller's permissions: a tool the caller cannot use is absent rather than refused, as the protocol allows (the tool set "MAY vary by the authorization presented on the request"). A principal who can write nowhere never sees workflow.commit: a smaller attack surface and a smaller context window.

Decision

A client authors by committing. workflow.commit makes a real git commit, attributed to the calling principal and marked as arriving through MCP, so git log and the audit log agree. Nothing changes a workflow without a commit. workflow.validate lets a client iterate without landing broken ones; the pre-receive hook is the backstop.

Teaching a client the language

workflow.language takes an optional topic and returns a page, not a manual: summary, keywords, the schema fragment governing them, worked examples. Without a topic it returns an orientation, a complete minimal workflow and the topics, which are the sections of the language: repository, inputs, outputs, triggers, steps, ports, needs, merge, fan_out, retry, expressions, secrets, files, script, includes, mcp.

Decision

The language documentation is generated from the schema, never written beside it. workflow.language projects the description and examples of every keyword in the JSON Schema of agentiik/schemas, and the build fails if a keyword lacks them. Two hand-kept sources would drift, into the worst failure available: a tool confidently teaching a model syntax the pre-receive hook then rejects.

Decision

A validation error is written for the reader that acts on it: a JSON Pointer to the offending node, what was expected there, and the workflow.language topic that covers it. The command line and the console show the same errors, so no audience gets a worse explanation.

A workflow as an MCP server

At /mcp/{namespace}/{workflow}, only if the entry point says so. Publishing the workflow as tools sets out the block key by key.

in agentiik.yaml
mcp:
  name: invoicing
  description: Issue invoices and check their status.

  tools:
    - name: create_invoice
      title: Create an invoice
      description: >
        Create one invoice for a customer and return its number and total.
        Rejects a customer whose VAT number does not validate.
      input:
        from: { input: orders }        # its JSON Schema becomes inputSchema
      output:
        from: { output: invoices }     # its envelope becomes structuredContent
      mode: sync
      timeout: 60s
      annotations:
        readOnlyHint: false
        idempotentHint: false

    - name: reconcile_month
      description: Reconcile a whole month. Long running; returns a run to follow.
      input:
        from: { input: period }
      mode: async
DeclaredBecomes, on the wire
input.frominputSchema: the input's own JSON Schema, as it stands, so no second schema can drift.
output.fromoutputSchema when the output declares a schema. Its envelope goes in structuredContent, with a text rendering alongside.
mode: syncWaits for the run and returns the output, for 120 seconds at most, because clients time out. A workflow that cannot finish inside that must be async.
mode: asyncReturns the run identifier at once, to follow with the platform server's run.get. A workflow's own server never grows a polling tool.
  • A tool call is a run: the calling principal's, with trigger_kind: mcp, in the run list, under the namespace quota and the workflow's concurrency group. A client calling in a loop meets the rate limit a webhook would.
  • Listing and calling both require workflow:run, never workflow:read.
Decision

The MCP surface is declared, never inferred: nothing about a tool comes from the graph. Inference would leak a workflow's internals to every caller and tie a published interface to internal refactors. So operator, the role without workflow:read, is exactly a client's grant: it lists and calls the tools and cannot read the entry point, the steps or the endpoints they talk to.

Decision

A workflow's server exposes tools and nothing else: no resources, no prompts, no tree. A resource would turn workflow:run into a read path into the repository, undoing the separation the roles were built around.

Errors and obligations

CaseAnswer
the run failsA tool execution error, isError: true, naming the failing step, its exit code and its message: the specification says clients should hand those to the model so it can correct itself.
an argument is malformedA protocol error. The input schema rejects it before any run exists.
The protocol requiresMet by
Validate all tool inputsThe input's JSON Schema, before a run exists.
Implement proper access controlsThe permission model. An unauthorised tool is not even listed.
Rate limit tool invocationsThe namespace quota and the concurrency group, as for every trigger.
Sanitize tool outputsSecret masking, as in logs: a secret never appears in a result. Above a size ceiling, the result is a reference to an artifact rather than the artifact.
§

Terraform provider

The provider writes down and applies what an installation is besides its workflows, rather than leaving it clicked and remembered. It is a client of /api/v1 with no authority of its own: a plan applies as the presenting principal, refused by the same grants as the console, so nothing is possible through Terraform that is not possible through the API.

ResourceManages
agentiik_namespaceName, kind, owner, quotas, allowed runner pools. Administrator only, like the route behind it.
agentiik_workflowThe repository: existence, default branch, that branch's protection. Not its contents.
agentiik_grantOne principal and scope, with a role or a deny naming one permission, and optional expiry. What a review is actually about.
agentiik_groupDefinition and membership.
agentiik_service_accountA non-human principal, its label, its owning namespace.
agentiik_api_tokenA service account's token, scope and expiry. The clear value is returned once, at creation; write-only.
agentiik_secretOne secret a namespace declares: provider and path, never the value. The workflow file only names it. Needs secret:write.
agentiik_runThat a run of a workflow, at a version, with given inputs, has happened. See Running a workflow.
Data sourceReads
agentiik_namespaceAn existing namespace, for a module adding to one it does not own.
agentiik_workflowDefault branch head, resolved graph at that commit, declared inputs and outputs.
agentiik_brickA catalog manifest (ports, parameters, digest), to pin an image by the digest a workflow was written against.
agentiik_runner_poolLabels and capacity, so allowed pools are written against what exists.
agentiik_run_outputOne output envelope of one run. Needs run:read_data; sensitive, since what it reads lands in the state file.
an environment, as HCL
terraform {
  required_providers {
    agentiik = {
      source  = "agentiik/agentiik"
      version = "~> 1.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "agentiik" {
  endpoint = "https://agentiik.example.com"
  # token from AGENTIIK_TOKEN; one written here is refused
}

resource "agentiik_namespace" "finance" {
  name  = "finance"
  kind  = "shared"
  owner = "group:finance-leads"

  quotas {
    max_concurrent_tasks = 20
    max_runs_per_hour    = 500
    max_artifact_bytes   = 500 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024
    max_retention_days   = 180
    allowed_runner_pools = ["default", "dmz"]
  }
}

resource "agentiik_workflow" "invoicing" {
  namespace      = agentiik_namespace.finance.name
  name           = "monthly-invoicing"
  default_branch = "main"

  protection {
    require_validation = true # the pre-receive hook; refusing to disable it is the point
    allow_force_push   = false
  }
}

resource "agentiik_grant" "ops_runs_invoicing" {
  principal  = "group:team-ops"
  scope      = agentiik_workflow.invoicing.id
  role       = "operator" # runs it; reads neither the file nor the steps
  expires_at = "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

What the provider does not manage

A deliberate boundary, not a roadmap item.

Stays outWhyInstead
a workflow's contentsHCL would be a second source of truth beside agentiik.yaml, disagreeing with it at the first push.git push, through the same hook as every push. The provider stops at the repository's first commit.
secret valuesA value passing through Terraform is a value in the state file, and treating the state as a secret store is how secrets most often escape infrastructure code.The declaration only: which provider, which path. A builtin value is written by its own PUT, outside Terraform.

Starting a run is in, but only in a shape that keeps an apply idempotent: see Running a workflow.

State, drift and authentication

  • Authentication is an API token in AGENTIIK_TOKEN, of a service account holding exactly the grants the configuration touches. A token written as a plain attribute is refused: that file is committed by construction.
  • agentiik_api_token returns its clear value once, into the state. Marking it sensitive hides it from output, not from the state file, so a configuration creating tokens needs an encrypted backend, as the resource's own documentation says.
  • Every resource can be imported, since the first real use is always an existing installation, by the API's identifier: finance for a namespace, finance/monthly-invoicing for a workflow, the grant identifier for a grant.
  • Drift is read back on refresh. A grant added in the console shows as a change to revert: if access is managed here, access granted elsewhere is drift.
  • The provider tracks the API version, not the core's: it declares the /api/v1 it speaks and refuses an endpoint answering another version, rather than failing halfway through an apply.

Running a workflow

Starting a run is an effect, and Terraform promises that a second apply changes nothing. So agentiik_run declares a state, not an act: a run of this workflow, at this version, with these inputs, has happened. Where that is already true, an apply does nothing.

a run as a state, and one as an action (the action requires Terraform 1.14)
resource "agentiik_workflow" "migrate_ledger" {
  namespace = agentiik_namespace.finance.name
  name      = "migrate-ledger"
}

resource "agentiik_run" "migrate" {
  workflow = agentiik_workflow.migrate_ledger.id
  ref      = "v2.1.0" # resolved to a commit at plan time
  inputs = {
    dry_run = false
  }

  wait       = "15m"    # a failed run fails the apply; false returns on acceptance
  on_destroy = "cancel" # default: a run still going is left to finish

  # anything here joins the identity: change it and a new run happens
  triggers = {
    schema_version = var.schema_version
  }
}

data "agentiik_run_output" "report" {
  run    = agentiik_run.migrate.id
  output = "report" # needs run:read_data, and lands in the state
}

action "agentiik_run" "reindex" {
  config {
    workflow = agentiik_workflow.search.id
    ref      = "v3.0.0"
    inputs   = { full = true }
  }
}

resource "agentiik_workflow" "search" {
  namespace = agentiik_namespace.finance.name
  name      = "search-index"

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.agentiik_run.reindex]
    }
  }
}

The run's identity is the workflow, the commit, the inputs and the triggers. The commit enters it, not the ref, so a plan that shows nothing means nothing will happen.

Since the last applyPlanOn the server
nothing changedno changeNo run, however many times the plan is applied.
workflow, inputs or triggers changedreplaceA new run.
ref now resolves to another commitreplaceA new run, shown in the plan rather than as a silent re-run.
resource destroyeddeleteNothing. A run that happened cannot be made not to have happened, so terraform destroy only forgets it.
destroyed while the run is goingdeleteLeft to finish, because cancelling somebody's half-done work on the way out of a destroy would surprise more. on_destroy = "cancel" cancels it.
  • wait holds the apply until the run settles, and a failed run fails the apply, naming the step, its exit code and what was refused, in that order. With wait = false the outputs stay empty, so a configuration reading them has to wait.
  • The resource exports the run identifier, state, timings and one envelope digest per output. Contents come from agentiik_run_output, sensitive because an output read into state is written to the state file.
  • It is a run like any other: the token's principal, trigger_kind: terraform, the run list, the namespace quota, the workflow's concurrency group. It needs only workflow:run, so operator is the grant and the provider never reads the file it runs.

Invoking one without declaring it

For an imperative run (reindex after this deploy, replay this migration now), the provider also exposes a Terraform 1.14 action (reindex above). terraform apply -invoke=action.agentiik_run.reindex runs it alone: the closest thing to agk run inside Terraform and its credentials.

Decision

Two forms answer two questions. agentiik_run answers has this run happened: the run is part of what the environment is, like a migration for a schema version or a seed for a fresh namespace. The action answers run this now: the run is part of what is being done, like a reindex after a deploy. Swapping them either invents a state nobody wanted or loses the record that a run happened.

Decision

Neither form makes Terraform a scheduler. A monthly run is a schedule trigger in the entry point: visible to every reader of the workflow, surviving the loss of a state file, independent of anyone's pipeline running apply. The provider starts runs that belong to a change; a run that belongs to the calendar belongs to the workflow.

Decision

The provider targets Terraform and its registry, although licensing rejects the Business Source License Terraform has been under since 2023. A licence position governs what this project publishes, not what its users run: the provider is Apache-2.0, on an MPL-2.0 plugin framework, and nothing source-available enters it. Refusing the tool an operator already runs would only cost them a provider. OpenTofu implements the same plugin protocol and the provider does not exclude it, but the provider is not tested there and nothing is promised of it.

§

Design system

The web console, agk console, the two mobile applications and the public site share one set of tokens: one accent, one state ramp, two typefaces, one spacing unit. A value a client needs beyond them is a gap in the system, not a licence to invent one.

Colour rules

  • The accent is the only brand colour, and marks what is interactive: primary buttons, links, selection, the selected row's marker, port dots on the graph.
  • The state ramp is separate from the accent, except running, which borrows its hue because it is the live state. Hue is shared, form never is: a button is a solid fill with ink on it, a state an outlined pill with a dot.
  • No state is signalled by colour alone: each carries a dot and a word, and a step strip adds position and width.
  • Elevation is ground value plus a hairline, never a shadow, and four surface tokens are the whole vocabulary: sunken for code and payload panes, bg for the page, surface for panels and rails, raised for rows, controls and the active item.

Typography

RoleFaceSize and weight
wordmarkArchivo15px / 700, tracking -0.02em, lowercase
section titleArchivo13px / 600
navigationArchivo13px / 400, 500 when active
controlArchivo12.5px / 500
body and secondaryArchivo12px / 400
column headArchivo10.5px / 600, uppercase, tracking 0.09em
identifier and dataJetBrains Mono11 to 12.5px / 400, 500 on a name
code and payloadJetBrains Mono11px / 400, line height 18 to 19px

Two faces, no third, both from Google Fonts with a system fallback stack. Anything a person copies, types, diffs or matches against a log is monospaced: run identifiers, namespaces, workflow, step and port names, image digests, exit codes, timestamps, durations, permission names, YAML and JSON. Everything a person only reads is Archivo.

The mark

The mark is the graph reduced to three rows on the sixteen-unit grid the icons use: one bar in, two side by side, one out. It is one colour at three strengths, because it draws one run at three stages and not three separate things.

RuleValue
colourThe accent only, never tinted to suit a coloured ground.
groundsurface or bg, never a photograph.
clear spaceOne bar, four units, on every side.
lockupMark and lowercase wordmark on one optical centre, nine units apart. The wordmark is Archivo 700, never another face. Where the name is already on screen, the mark stands alone.
smallest size16 × 14, where it was drawn; the two-unit closing bar shuts below it. Larger sizes scale by whole units.
iconThe mark alone, never the lockup: a favicon or an application icon has no room for a wordmark.
neverOutlined, boxed, rotated, gradient-filled, or given a fourth row.

Density and rhythm

MeasureValue
base unit2px. Common gaps are 6, 8, 10, 14 and 18.
top bar52px, holding the mark, the namespace switcher, the views, search, notifications and the principal. There is no sidebar, so the panes take the window's width, as in agk console. Sub-navigation and filter bars 48px. The console assumes a window of at least 1280px.
paneA surface bordered at 1px with 7px corners, its title set into the top border, the pane in focus bordered in the accent.
key line32px at the foot of the window: the keys of the view, each named by its effect, as agk console's bottom line names them.
table row44px, header 34px, footer 40px.
content padding18px on the page, 14px inside a panel.
radii3px state pill, 4px role and code chip, 5px control, 6px graph node and inner panel, 7px card, fully round on filter chips and on workflow input and output chips.
borders1px everywhere. 1.5px is reserved for a graph node and 2.5px for the element that carries the current focus.

Iconography

  • Stroke only, on a 16px grid at 1.5px, round caps and joins, no fill and no two-tone.
  • An icon takes muted, or the colour of the state it carries, and then always comes with a word.
  • No emoji, in any surface of the product.

Voice

  • Sentence case throughout, buttons, tabs and headings included.
  • A control names its effect: Approve, Reject, Replay from invoice, Load 25 more. Never OK, never Submit.
  • An error names the step, the exit code and what was refused, in that order.
  • Identifiers are never translated or prettified: run:read_data, rejected, succeeded appear as the YAML and the API spell them, so what a person reads on screen is what they type in a file.
Decision

The mobile applications inherit the tokens, the type roles and the voice, not the density. A phone raises every hit target to at least 44 points and turns tables into card lists rather than shrinking the console. A shared palette is a system; a shared layout is a compromise that serves neither client.

§

Web console

ViewWhat it shows or does
graphPorts and edges exactly as declared, with live per-step state during a run.
visual editorTwo-way editing of one object model, serialised by the same writer as the command line.
run inspectorPer step: input envelope, output envelope per port, logs, resolved parameters, image digest, and the runner that executed the task.
sharing panelOn every workflow and namespace: who holds what, where each permission comes from, what one person can actually do. One control adds, expires or denies.
repository browserThe tree at any ref, and a branch switcher to run a change before merging it.
diffTwo commits, over the whole tree and not only the entry point, or two runs of the same commit.
statisticsCharts of a workflow's runs, steps and ports, of a namespace against its quotas and, for administrators, of the pools and runners (Statistics).
brick catalogManifests, parameter schemas, published examples.
MCP panelOn a workflow that declares one: the endpoint URL, and the tools exactly as a client sees them, schemas rendered from the declaration.
namespace switcherIn the top bar: the personal namespace first, shared ones grouped after it.
credentialsEnrol, name and remove passkeys, with each one's last use. An administrator sees every user's list, and whether each credential is synced or device-bound.
  • A format-preserving YAML tree keeps the file's comments and key order, so a round trip through the editor leaves no spurious diff in review.
  • Payload panes are hidden, not merely disabled, for a principal without run:read_data.
  • Removing a credential is refused when it would drop the account below the policy's minimum.
  • The views a terminal serves well are also agk console, over the same routes: Terminal console.

The web console is served on the API's origin: at the root of the public URL, with the API under /api/v1 and the sign-in page under /auth. Whether the API serves the console's files itself or a console container sits behind the same proxy path is for v0.6.0's deployment to settle; a second origin is not.

Decision

One origin for the console and the API, rather than a console on a host of its own sharing a registrable domain with the API, which WebAuthn would allow. Passkeys, the session cookie and the Origin check each need the same origin, and three things kept in step across two hosts is where one of them drifts. The Relying Party Identifier, the public URL's host since v0.3.0, then never changes, as changing it would invalidate every passkey enrolled; and one URL is what a person remembers.

The web console is drawn in agk console's design language, in a browser. The panes are bordered with rounded corners on the palette's quiet surfaces, each titled in its top border and the one in focus in the accent; a state is a badge in its colour with a dot and its word; identifiers, digests, times and logs are monospaced; a top bar holds the namespace switcher, the views and the principal; the graph is boxes and edges with its live state and a fan-out's shards and bar; notifications arrive as toasts; and a key line at the foot of the window names the keys of the view. What a browser adds, it keeps:

The browser addsBecause
the mouse firstA pointer is how a browser is used, so every act is a button or a link (Approve, Replay from invoice, Cancel run), a mark explains itself under the pointer, and the keys of the key line are shortcuts beside them rather than the only way.
formsAdding a grant, a manual run's inputs drawn from their JSON Schemas, and a namespace's settings are forms the browser checks before anything is sent.
the visual editorEditing the graph and the file as one object model needs a canvas to drag one port onto another; agk console leaves editing to the clone.
passkeysSigning in and enrolling are ceremonies a browser runs (Authentication).
Decision

The web console and agk console share one design language, where the web console was first drawn with a sidebar and tables of its own. They are one product: the same runs, the same states in the same colours, the same graph, the same principal's permissions. An operator who moves between them, the browser at a desk and agk console over SSH at night, reads the same thing in the same place, and a state learnt in one is recognised in the other; two languages would be two products to learn, each change to one leaving the other behind. The browser keeps what it does better, since a shared language is not a shared lowest common denominator.

Decision

YAML stays the source of truth even when editing happens in the console. A graph store exporting YAML would make review in a Git repository illusory, and the two would diverge at the first feature with no visual equivalent. The sharing panel is the one part of the console with no YAML counterpart, by design.

Statistics

For whoever wants the numbers behind the runs, the web console draws them as charts: a workflow's and its steps', a namespace's against its quotas and, to an administrator, the pools' and the runners'. Each chart is a series an aggregate route of the API answers (API and command line), computed where the runs are recorded, and agk console draws the compact form of the same series.

OfSeriesDrawn as
a workflowIts runs by final state, and the share of each bucket that did not succeed; the p50, p95 and p99 of their duration; the queue wait of their tasks, from creation to dispatch; the attempts retried, by exit code.stacked columns, lines, bars
a stepIts duration by weekday and hour; its exit codes; the items on each of its ports and the share rejected or sent to error; a fan-out's throughput, in items a minute while its shards run.a heatmap, bars, lines
a namespaceThe runs created in each hour, and those refused with 429, against max_runs_per_hour; the tasks in flight against max_concurrent_tasks; the artifact bytes against max_artifact_bytes, and what each day added.columns, a line, an area, each under its limit
a pool, a runnerTo an administrator alone: the slots in use against the capacity, which falls as a runner drains; each silence between heartbeats longer than two intervals, 20 s, those of 30 s and more, after which a runner's tasks are declared lost, set apart.a line over a step line, a timeline
ControlWhat it does
rangeThe last hour, 24 hours, 7, 30 or 90 days, or a span chosen, for every chart of the page at once. The bucket follows the range, so that a chart holds a few hundred points at most: a minute up to two hours, 15 minutes up to two days, an hour up to 14 days, a day beyond.
zoomDragging across a chart narrows the range to that span, for every chart; a double click steps back.
readoutUnder the pointer, the bucket's bounds and the exact value of each series; on a column, a cell or a mark, that one's.
comparisonThe same span before the range, dashed behind it, and the change beside each figure.
exportThe series behind the page as CSV or JSON: the numbers the route answered, never the picture.
a pointA click opens the runs it counts: the runs view filtered by workflow, state and the bucket's bounds, as GET /api/v1/runs takes them.
  • A series counts only what the caller may read: the runs of the workflows it holds run:read on, as GET /api/v1/runs lists them, so a chart shows nothing a list would not. It carries counts, durations and exit codes, never an item, so run:read_data is never asked. A namespace's quota series go to whoever reads the namespace, and the pools and runners to administrators alone.
  • The browser never reads Prometheus: the controller's metrics stay the operator's, on the operator's network.
  • A series is computed from the run, task and artifact records rather than kept apart, so a range reaches back as far as the namespace keeps its runs, and no further.
  • Colour follows the state a series counts, as everywhere in the console, and a series that is no state is drawn in the accent, in strengths of the one hue. Every chart has its legend and a table of its numbers, so no series is told by colour alone.
  • agk console shows the compact form, from the same routes: a workflow's sparkline of its last twenty runs and, beside it, a small histogram of its durations over the range (Live state and notifications). The charts stay the browser's.
Decision

Statistics are served by aggregate routes of the API rather than read from Prometheus or computed in the browser. An aggregate over runs discloses the runs, so it answers to the same grants: the API filters it by run:read as it filters GET /api/v1/runs, where a metrics endpoint knows no principal and sets every namespace's series side by side for whoever reaches it. Computed once, where the runs are recorded, a p95 is one number in the web console, in agk console, on a phone and in a script, where clients each paging through runs to compute their own would disagree, and none could page through a hundred thousand. And no metrics endpoint is opened to a browser: Prometheus stays on the operator's network, and an installation that runs none still has its charts.

§

Terminal console

The web console's views, in a terminal, drawn to be worth opening. agk console fills the screen with panes side by side, the graph drawn as boxes and edges, states in the design system's colours, spinners, progress bars and sparklines, the mouse beside the keys, a filter that answers as you type and a command palette. It is for whoever works over SSH or would rather not leave the shell, and it arrives in v0.6.0, beside the web console; every figure in this chapter is a mockup of what that release builds.

ItemWhat it is
serverNone. agk console is agk, speaking to /api/v1 as agk logs and agk status do: nothing to install, open or turn on at the installation.
routesThe ones the web console reads, and no other. Nothing is added to the API for it.
principalThe one agk is signed in as: the token agk login stored, or AGENTIIK_TOKEN, against --server or AGENTIIK_SERVER (Pointing agk at an installation).
permissionsNone of its own. It shows what the principal holds, as GET /api/v1/me gives it, and hides the rest rather than disabling it, payload panes included without run:read_data. A token narrowed by a scope narrows the console with it.
opens onThe runs view of every namespace the principal reads; --namespace NS on one namespace; agk console RUN on that run.
exits0 when quit. 2 for a wrong command line and 4 where the installation cannot be reached at start, as every verb. Once open, an installation that stops answering is said so in the top line and asked again, since somebody is watching.
Decision

A verb, agk console, rather than agk --console, which is how the idea first came. Everything agk does is a verb, as agk logs and agk status are, and a flag changes how a verb does it, as --local and -o json do. A flag standing for a verb would be a second grammar for the reader of agk's help to learn, and it would leave the console's own flags, --namespace among them, nothing to belong to.

Decision

The terminal console is a client of the API, not something an installation serves: no SSH server, no port, no route and no permission is added for it. Served by the installation, it would be a second way in with a sign-in of its own, and a rule it applied would be one the API does not enforce. As a client, it shows nothing the principal could not ask the API for, which is what makes it safe to add at all.

Decision

The screen is drawn with Charm's Bubble Tea, Lip Gloss and Bubbles, although the project reaches for the standard library first. A terminal interface worth using needs a renderer that redraws only what changed, a layout engine that measures and joins styled blocks, and input handling that decodes keys, the mouse, resizes and the terminal's answers about itself. The standard library has none of the three, and golang.org/x/term gives a raw mode and a window size, not a screen; written here, they would be a terminal toolkit of the project's own to maintain, where Bubble Tea is the one Go's terminal applications are built and kept up on. The dependency is recorded in go.mod with that reason, and it stays inside cmd/agk: the test that holds the graph evaluator and the container driver to no server, no bus and no database refuses them any Charm package too, so agk run --local stays the same code path it was.

Panes and layout

The panes are laid out from the window's size, again at every resize, so one screen serves a wide monitor and an SSH session opened at its default size.

WindowPanes
160 columns and moreRuns, run and log side by side, as above. With no run open, the runs take the whole width, one line a run with more columns; opening a run adds the two panes on its right.
120 to 159 columnsRuns beside the run, and the log beneath the run in the lower third of its column.
under 120 columnsStacked, below. Once a run is open, the runs fold to one line that still counts the failed and the running; the run and its log share the rows, the pane in focus taking two thirds.
under 80 columns or 24 rowsNothing drawn cut: the window is asked to grow, naming the size it needs.
  • tab moves the focus to the next pane, and a click does too. The pane in focus has the accent's border, as selection does in the web console.
  • A border between two panes side by side is dragged with the mouse to move it, for the rest of the session.
  • A pane is filled with the palette's surface and bordered with rounded corners, as Lip Gloss draws them; the three panes above are three such blocks joined.

Views

The web console's views where a terminal serves them well, each reading what the web console reads.

ViewWhat it shows or doesReads
runsNewest first and kept live: state, run, workflow, trigger, start, duration and principal, and at full width a strip of the run's steps and a sparkline of its workflow's last twenty runs. Failed runs, and from v0.8.0 waiting ones, sit in a band above the list, since they are why it is opened. Filtered as you type (Keys and the mouse).GET /api/v1/runs
runIts graph drawn, each step's state live, a fan-out's shards one cell each beside a bar of those done. A step's exit code and its meaning, attempt, shard, image digest, runner name, pool and labels, never the host. Each port's envelope with its item count, and its JSON under run:read_data, up to the size rules. Its log, history then live, as agk logs follows it. Cancel, replay from a step and, from v0.8.0, approve or reject.GET /api/v1/runs/{id}, its steps' inputs, outputs and logs
graphThe resolved graph of a run or a version, full screen, drawn as boxes and edges (The graph, drawn), or written as a list.GET /api/v1/{ns}/workflows/{name}
workflowsThe workflows of a namespace the principal can read, each one's versions, declared triggers, a sparkline of its last twenty runs and a histogram of its durations, and a version's graph.what the web console lists, GET /api/v1/{ns}/workflows/{name}, GET /api/v1/runs and GET /api/v1/{ns}/stats/runs
sharingWhat agk grants prints, kept live, for a workflow or a namespace: the grants as written, and resolved for one principal with the scope each permission comes from, a deny the only subtraction.GET /api/v1/{ns}/grants, GET /api/v1/{ns}/workflows/{name}/grants
runnersTo an administrator alone: runners and pools, with labels, capacity, last heartbeat, state and concurrency, and who drained or revoked one and when, never a host.GET /api/v1/runners, GET /api/v1/runner-pools

The graph, drawn

The graph is drawn as the web console draws it, in the terminal's own characters: each step a box with rounded corners, ╭─╮, and each edge a line of ─ and │, its turns rounded, ending in an arrowhead where it arrives.

ElementDrawn as
stepA box: its state's glyph and its name, then its state and duration, and for a fan_out one cell per shard in its state, a bar of those done and the count, 11/16. merge and when are written inside it.
edgeNamed at the port it leaves, with the item count once the port has published: ok 328.
rejectedDashed, in the waiting amber: items a step refused and passed on, not a failure.
errorIn the failed red: a port for what failed, which ends nothing by itself.
any other portThe muted line.
workflow input or outputA pill at the edge of the drawing.
selected stepA heavier border. enter opens it in the inspector.
layoutLayers in an order the graph runs in, ties broken by name. Left to right in a pane wider than tall, as below, top to bottom otherwise, as in the run pane above; each layer ordered against the one before, to keep crossings few.
a graph larger than its panePans to keep the selected step in view as the keys move it, and with the mouse wheel; it never shrinks.
Decision

The graph is drawn, where this chapter first wrote it as a list. A list fits any window, but it leaves the reader to build the shape in their head, and the shape is what a person at a failed run looks at first: which branch, which fan-out, what came after it. The drawing needs room, so it pans rather than shrinking past reading. The list stays one key away, g, for a graph too large to take in drawn and for a screen reader, which reads a list and not a picture made of box-drawing characters; it is also what the console prints for a graph where there is no terminal.

g in the graph view: the same graph as a list, the example of The graph and its ports, mid-run
inputs      orders, customers  -> normalize
normalize   succeeded  1.2s
  ok        -> invoice   in
  rejected  -> archive   rejected
invoice     running    3 of 8 shards done  fan_out: item
  out       -> archive   invoices
  error     -> output    errors
archive     queued
  out       -> output    invoices

Written as a list, the graph runs in an order it runs in, each edge under the step it leaves, naming the port, the step or workflow output it reaches and that one's port, so nothing is read off the direction of a line.

Live state and notifications

What changes while the console is open is shown changing, and nothing moves that is not live: an animation on something settled would teach the eye to ignore the ones that matter.

SignShowsFrom
spinnerBeside every running run, step and shard, in the accent's hue, beside the word running.the runs and the run, as they are read
shard cells and barOn a fan_out: one cell per shard in its state, and a bar of those done.GET /api/v1/runs/{id}
sparklineThe durations of a workflow's last twenty runs, one bar each, oldest first: a failure in red, the run in progress in the accent, the rest muted, beside their median.GET /api/v1/runs, narrowed by workflow and limit
histogramA workflow's durations over the last 30 days, a dozen bins drawn in block characters, its p50 and p95 marked, beside its sparkline in the workflows view: the compact form of the web console's statistics.GET /api/v1/{ns}/stats/runs, with histogram
liveIn the top line, a green dot and the word while the installation answers; in words, and asked again, when it stops.every read
toastA notification, in the corner, over the panes.GET /api/v1/me, and the runs view
  • A toast is a notification GET /api/v1/me holds that arrived while the console is open, read again every 30 seconds, or the end of a run the principal started, seen in the runs the console already reads. Half a minute late costs nothing for a notice kept 90 days, and costs the API one small read.
  • Notifications already waiting at start are counted in the top line and not toasted, so opening the console never buries the screen.
  • A toast stays eight seconds and never takes the focus: a key pressed while one shows goes where it was going, since a toast that took keys would swallow the y of a prompt. A click on it opens what it names.
  • The palette's Notifications lists every one, and dismisses one with DELETE /api/v1/me/notifications/{id}.

Keys and the mouse

KeyDoes
↑ ↓ or j kMoves the selection; in a graph, to the step above or below.
← → or h lIn a graph, moves the selection to the step before or after, along an edge.
enterOpens what is selected: a run, a step, a workflow, a version.
escGoes back to the view before, or closes the filter, the palette or a prompt.
tab shift+tabMoves the focus to the next or the previous pane: in a run, steps, ports, then log.
1 to 4Runs, workflows, sharing, and runners for an administrator.
/Filters the list as you type, below.
:Opens the command palette, below.
gOpens the graph of the selected run or version; in the graph, writes it as a list and back.
[ ]The previous or next port of the step in the inspector.
cCancels the selected run, once a prompt naming it is answered y.
pReplays the run from the selected step, once a prompt naming both is answered y.
a rFrom v0.8.0, approves or rejects a waiting run, asking first for the approval's optional comment or the rejection's reason.
?Lists every key of the view.
qQuits, from any view.
MouseDoes
clickSelects a row, a step, a port or a tab, and focuses its pane; on a toast, opens what it names.
double clickOpens what it selects, as enter does.
wheelScrolls the list or the log under the pointer, or pans the graph.
drag a borderMoves the border between two panes.
shift and dragSelects text as the terminal does, to copy a run identifier or a log line: a terminal gives the mouse back to itself while shift is held, and the console asking for the mouse would otherwise take copying away.

The mouse's reports reach agk as the keys do, in the terminal's own escape sequences, so it works over SSH as it does locally. Every mouse action has a key, and no key needs the mouse.

The filter

/ opens a line above the list, and each key narrows the list at once:

  • A word matches its letters in order against a run's identifier, workflow, state, trigger and principal, the closest matches first: inv fail.
  • A name=value term is one GET /api/v1/runs takes, namespace, workflow, state, since and until, with since also taking a duration back from now: state=failed since=24h. It is sent when typing pauses for a quarter of a second, since the list holds only the runs loaded and a filter over those alone would miss older ones; the words then match within what the installation answered.
  • enter keeps the filter and returns to the list, esc clears it.

The command palette

: opens the palette over whatever is on screen: every command of the view and every view, and every run, workflow and namespace the principal reads, by name or by the start of an identifier, matched as the filter matches. It opens on the five commands used last. It uses : because vim and k9s open their command line with it, where people at a terminal already look.

  • The bottom line shows the keys of the view, each named by its effect, as a control is in the web console (Voice): c Cancel run, never c OK. The palette shows each command's key beside it, so a command found once is a keystroke the next time.
  • A key or a command for what the principal does not hold is left out of that line and of the palette, and does nothing, as the web console hides a control rather than disabling it.
  • A prompt defaults to no, so a key pressed twice by mistake stops at the question, and any key but y answers no.
  • From v0.8.0, with the wait step, a run waiting on an approval sits first in the band, and a opens the prompt below: the run, the step it waits at, what it holds, the optional comment, then the question.

Colour

The console draws in the design system's palette, the same greens, ambers and reds for the same states as the web console, and paints the palette's ground under what it draws, so the contrast the design system chose holds whatever the terminal's theme. The values are not typed into agk: they are generated into cmd/agk from the design repository's token file at the same version, so the terminal cannot drift from the browser. It degrades with what the terminal can show:

The terminalDrawsKnown from
true colourThe palette's values, exactly, on the palette's ground.COLORTERM is truecolor or 24bit
256 coloursEach token's nearest of the 256, by CIE Lab distance, on the nearest ground.TERM ends in 256color
16 coloursThe terminal's own named colours, below, and no painted ground.any other TERM
no colourNo colour and no ground; bold, faint and reverse still mark a heading, what is absent and the selection.NO_COLOR set and not empty
no screenPlain lines, as Where it runs says.not a terminal, or TERM=dumb
